title_en: New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade postponed due to weather
title_zh: 纽约梅西百货感恩节大游行因天气原因推迟
summary: Forecasters say high winds on Thursday may spoil the annual march of huge balloons and have moved the parade to Saturday New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade has been postponed due to excessively windy weather and will now be held on Saturday. Foreca
summary_zh: 预报员表示，周四的大风可能会破坏每年一度的巨型气球游行，并将游行移至周六纽约市的梅西百货感恩节
body_en: Forecasters say high winds on Thursday may spoil the annual march of huge balloons and have moved the parade to Saturday
New York City’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day parade has been postponed due to excessively windy weather and will now be held on Saturday.

Forecasters say an impending storm on Thursday may spoil the street party, which is marked by a march of huge balloons. AccuWeather is forecasting winds of 12 to 25 mph (19 to 40 km/h) and rain later on Thursday.
Under guidelines, large balloons must stay grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph (37 km/h) or gusts exceed 34 mph (55 km/h). The parade balloons have been grounded only once previously, in 1971.
NBC quoted Macy’s as saying: “The safety of our participants and spectators is our priority.”
Macy’s added: “Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

This year the parade will include a tribute to Dolly Parton led by Megan Hilty, and special appearances by Melissa Joan Hart, Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer and Holly Robinson Peete, all leading the way for Santa Claus. Nine Broadway shows will be featured as part of a 10-minute medley, replacing the traditional sprinkling of full show numbers.

The Macy’s parade began more than a century ago in 1924 as a way of creating buzz for the giant department store’s holiday windows at Macy’s Herald Square flagship store in Manhattan. Macy’s borrowed animals from the Central Park Zoo for the first parades but in 1927 ended that practice after children were getting scared.

The animals were then replaced with air-filled balloons and, a year later, balloons that could be filled with helium – a now familiar sight for people around the world from countless Hollywood movies set in New York City.

The parades have been fully cancelled previously only in 1942, 1943 and 1944 because the valuable materials needed to create the huge balloons were diverted for the the second world war effort against Germany and Japan.
body_zh: 预报员表示，周四的大风可能会破坏每年一度的巨型气球游行，并将游行移至周六
纽约市梅西百货感恩节游行因大风天气而推迟，现将于周六举行。
预报员表示，周四即将到来的暴风雨可能会破坏以巨大气球游行为标志的街头派对。 AccuWeather 预计周四晚些时候将有 12 至 25 英里/小时（19 至 40 公里/小时）的风速和降雨。
根据指导方针，如果持续风速超过 23 英里/小时（37 公里/小时）或阵风超过 34 英里/小时（55 公里/小时），大型气球必须保持接地。游行气球此前仅在 1971 年被接地过一次。
NBC援引梅西百货的话说：“参与者和观众的安全是我们的首要任务。”
梅西百货补充道：“感谢成千上万的志愿者、表演者和合作伙伴，他们每年创造了数百万人享受的魔法。我们期待着周六一起庆祝。”

今年的游行将包括由梅根·希尔蒂 (Megan Hilty) 领导的向多莉·帕顿 (Dolly Parton) 致敬的活动，以及梅丽莎·琼·哈特 (Melissa Joan Hart)、杰克·麦克布瑞尔 (Jack McBrayer)、珍妮特·麦克蒂尔 (Janet McTeer) 和霍莉·罗宾逊·皮特 (Holly Robinson Peete) 的特别亮相，他们都为圣诞老人带路。九场百老汇演出将作为 10 分钟混合表演的一部分，取代传统的散播完整演出的方式。
梅西百货游行始于一个多世纪前的 1924 年，目的是为曼哈顿梅西百货先驱广场旗舰店的大型百货商店假日橱窗制造热闹。梅西百货从中央公园动物园借来了动物进行首次游行，但在 1927 年孩子们感到害怕后终止了这种做法。
然后，这些动物被充气气球所取代，一年后，又被充满氦气的气球所取代——这是世界各地人们在无数以纽约为背景的好莱坞电影中熟悉的景象。
此前，仅在 1942 年、1943 年和 1944 年，阅兵式才被完全取消，因为制造巨型气球所需的宝贵材料被转用于第二次世界大战中对抗德国和日本的行动。

title_en: Oregon man and dog narrowly escape being swept away by high tides as officials urge caution at beaches
title_zh: 官员敦促海滩小心谨慎，俄勒冈州男子和狗险些被涨潮卷走
summary: Record-breaking king tides have prompted west coast authorities to warn residents to stay away from beaches The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have urged residents to avoid beaches, but not everyone is heeding those warn
summary_zh: 破纪录的大潮促使西海岸当局警告居民远离海滩 美国西海岸出现破纪录的大潮
body_en: Oregon man and dog narrowly escape being swept away by high tides as officials urge caution at beaches | West Coast
Record-breaking king tides have prompted west coast authorities to warn residents to stay away from beaches
The US west coast has seen record-breaking tides this week and authorities have urged residents to avoid beaches, but not everyone is heeding those warnings.

In Cannon Beach, Oregon , viral footage showed a man and his dog nearly getting swept away by a so-called king tide on Tuesday morning. The man had been standing on a staircase holding his leashed dog, who was walking in the sand, when the water suddenly surged, knocking him to his feet.
California on edge as high tides and floods set to wreak havoc over Thanksgiving. Here is what to know

They ultimately escaped without injury, according to the Cannon Beach police department. Earlier that morning, police had cited the same man for driving on the shoreline. He had reportedly “indicated” to an officer he wanted to get a better look at the high tides.
Other footage captured around Cannon Beach on Tuesday morning showed a jogger narrowly avoiding a major wave, while another stood amid the wave seemingly filming.

King tides are the highest tide cycles of the year. This winter, conditions caused by the super El Niño have pushed these tides to record levels, contributing to widespread flooding, powerful waves and coastal erosion.
The Cannon Beach police department advised residents to stay off beaches and keep pets away from the water.

“King tides are an impressive natural phenomenon, but no photograph, video or closer look is worth risking your life, the life of your pet or the lives of the first responders who may be called upon to rescue you,” the police department said in a statement.

A coastal flood advisory is in effect for the region through Thursday, according to the National Weather Service, as “king tides, elevated seas, and the arrival of fresh swells likely lead to tidal overflow”.
body_zh: 官员敦促海滩小心谨慎，俄勒冈州男子和狗险些被涨潮卷走西海岸
破纪录的大潮促使西海岸当局警告居民远离海滩
美国西海岸本周出现了破纪录的潮汐，当局敦促居民避开海滩，但并非所有人都注意到这些警告。
在俄勒冈州坎农海滩，一段疯传的视频显示，周二早上，一名男子和他的狗差点被所谓的大潮卷走。这名男子当时牵着拴着的狗站在楼梯上，狗在沙地上行走，突然水流汹涌，把他冲倒在地。
由于涨潮和洪水对感恩节造成严重破坏，加州陷入紧张状态。这是你需要知道的
据坎农海滩警察局称，他们最终逃脱，没有受伤。当天早上早些时候，警方指控同一名男子在海岸线上开车。据报道，他曾向一名官员“表示”他想更好地观察涨潮情况。
周二早上在坎农海滩附近拍摄的其他镜头显示，一名慢跑者险些避开了大浪，而另一名慢跑者则站在海浪中，似乎正在拍摄。
王潮是一年中最高的潮汐周期。今年冬天，超级厄尔尼诺现象导致潮汐达到创纪录水平，导致大面积洪水、巨浪和海岸侵蚀。
坎农海滩警察局建议居民远离海滩，并让宠物远离水面。
警察局在一份声明中表示：“大潮是一种令人印象深刻的自然现象，但任何照片、视频或近距离观察都不值得拿你的生命、你的宠物的生命或可能被要求营救你的急救人员的生命冒险。”
据国家气象局称，沿海洪水警告对该地区的影响持续到周四，因为“大潮、海平面上升和新涌浪的到来可能导致潮汐溢出”。

title_en: Smoke seen from a mile away as army detonates US stockpile of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa
title_zh: 当军队在爱荷华州引爆美国储存的炸弹制造化学品时，从一英里外就能看到烟雾
summary: Controlled blast to dispose of lead azide risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals in 100-mile radius The US army detonated the nation’s entire stockpile of the the bomb-making material lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning, despite an outpouring of public
summary_zh: 处理叠氮化铅的受控爆炸有可能在 100 英里半径范围内释放出大量有毒化学物质 美国军队引爆了该国的全部库存
body_en: Controlled blast to dispose of lead azide risks releasing plumes of toxic chemicals in 100-mile radius

The US army detonated the nation’s entire stockpile of the the bomb-making material lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday morning, despite an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.

The controlled blast, which took place at about 10.00am ET, was to dispose of 9,700lb (4,400kg) of the chemical that was stored at the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa that is home to about 400 people.
The explosion risked releasing plumes of toxic chemicals in a 100-mile (160km) radius, but exactly where those toxins will land has changed with the weather forecast.

Images taken from a distance away appeared to show a white plume of smoke rising over the town immediately after the blast, before dissipating quickly. One local news station, KWQC, reported seeing a large amount of smoke from more than a mile away.
A local reporter in Iowa , who was live on air when the detonation happened, said he heard “a big boom” and and could “actually visibly see the shockwave coming through”.

Others were less impressed by the size of the blast. Tim Brandt, a resident of Burlington, Iowa, told the Associated Press that he wanted to see a big boom and feel the ground shake, but that instead, the detonation reminded him of the noisemakers that crack when thrown on the ground.
“It was nothing,” he said. “It seemed like government put fear in a lot of people over nothing.”
Shortly after the detonation, Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social that “early reports from Iowa are that the Army’s mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations”.
A map showing forecasted potential for lead dust where healthy limits are exceeded
Lee Zeldin, head of the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), said that he has been told that the blast “caved inward perfectly”.

He said: “When the army was planning its mitigation efforts, there were a number of actions that were taken that included an effort to get the detonation to go… downland and toward unoccupied land within the Iowa army ammunition plant.”
“This message that I just received … First off, the air monitors are showing a remaining zero detection, and as far as the blast itself, it caved inward perfectly.”

The EPA added in a statement that “real-time air monitors are reporting ZERO detection of airborne lead throughout the region” and that monitors “never stopped collecting data throughout the event”. The agency also launched a website through which visitors can monitor live air quality readings along the plume route.
The acting army secretary, Adam Telle, said that that “the threat of an uncontrolled spontaneous detonation has been eliminated”.

“I am so proud of our SOLDIERS for their courage, training, mitigation and precision! They put it on the line for all of us just like this every day!” he said in a statement. Telle also thanked Trump and his administration “for mobilizing an unprecedented whole of government approach to fix this problem once and for all for the great people of Iowa”.

Lead azide, which typically appears as a white powder or needle-like crystals, is a explosive chemical compound of lead used mainly in detonators, according to the National Center for Biotechnology Information .

The US army said that a routine inspection in March at the Iowa facility found that “decades-old, stored lead azide had partially crystallized, making it increasingly sensitive to friction, shock and cold winter temperatures”.

The army said that the deterioration had “created a new and growing risk of spontaneous, uncontrolled detonation.” The army described lead azide as a “highly sensitive explosive” which becomes “increasingly unstable as it deteriorates”.
body_zh: 处理叠氮化铅的受控爆炸可能会在 100 英里半径范围内释放有毒化学物质
尽管公众对潜在的健康和环境影响表示担忧，但美国军队周三上午在爱荷华州引爆了该国全部库存的炸弹制造材料叠氮化铅。
这次受控爆炸发生在美国东部时间上午 10 点左右，目的是处理储存在位于米德尔敦的爱荷华州陆军弹药厂的 9,700 磅（4,400 公斤）化学品。米德尔敦是爱荷华州东南部的一个小镇，约有 400 人居住。
爆炸有可能在 100 英里（160 公里）半径范围内释放有毒化学物质，但这些毒素的确切降落地点已随天气预报而变化。
从远处拍摄的图像似乎显示，爆炸发生后，城镇上空立即升起一股白色烟雾，然后迅速消散。当地一家新闻台 KWQC 报道说，看到一英里多外冒出大量烟雾。
爆炸发生时，一名正在现场直播的爱荷华州当地记者表示，他听到“一声巨响”，并且“实际上可以看到冲击波传来”。
其他人对爆炸的规模不太感兴趣。爱荷华州伯灵顿居民蒂姆·勃兰特告诉美联社，他希望看到一声巨响并感受到地面震动，但爆炸却让他想起了扔在地上时发出的噪音。
“没什么，”他说。 “政府似乎无缘无故地让很多人感到恐惧。”
爆炸发生后不久，唐纳德·特朗普在《真相社会》的一篇帖子中表示，“来自爱荷华州的早期报告显示，陆军的缓解努力远远超出了预期”。
一张地图显示了超过健康限度的铅尘预测潜力
美国环境保护署（EPA）局长李泽尔丁表示，他被告知爆炸“完全向内塌陷”。
他说：“当军队计划缓解措施时，采取了许多行动，其中包括努力让爆炸发生……低地和爱荷华州陆军弹药厂内未占领的土地。”
“我刚刚收到的消息……首先，空中监视器显示剩余的零探测，就爆炸本身而言，它完美地向内塌陷。”
美国环保署在一份声明中补充说，“实时空气监测仪报告称，整个地区空气中铅的检测为零”，并且监测仪“在整个事件期间从未停止收集数据”。该机构还推出了一个网站，游客可以通过该网站监测羽流沿线的实时空气质量读数。
代理陆军部长亚当·泰勒表示，“失控自爆的威胁已经消除”。
“我为我们的士兵感到非常自豪，他们的勇气、训练、缓解和精准！他们每天都像这样为我们所有人冒着风险！”他在一份声明中说。泰勒还感谢特朗普和他的政府“动员了前所未有的整体政府方法，为伟大的爱荷华州人民一劳永逸地解决这个问题”。
据国家生物技术信息中心称，叠氮化铅通常呈白色粉末或针状晶体，是一种主要用于雷管的爆炸性铅化合物。
美国军方表示，三月份对爱荷华州设施的例行检查发现，“储存了数十年的叠氮化铅已部分结晶，使其对摩擦、冲击和冬季寒冷的温度越来越敏感”。
军方表示，局势恶化“造成了新的、日益严重的自发、不受控制爆炸的风险”。军方将叠氮化铅描述为“高度敏感的爆炸物”，“随着恶化而变得越来越不稳定”。

body_en: 53 incoming House Democrats to boycott Harvard orientation in support of graduate students’ strike | Harvard University
‘We have been informed that to attend your event we would be required to cross a union picket line,’ the Democrats say

Fifty-three newly elected members of Congress told Harvard University on Tuesday that they will boycott an informal orientation program at Harvard’s Kennedy School next month in support of the school’s striking graduate students union .

In a letter to the university’s administrators, the incoming House Democrats expressed thanks for their invitations to the Bipartisan Program for Newly Elected Members of Congress, in which more than 800 members have participated since 1972.

“However, as much as we would like to attend, we have been informed that to attend your event we would be required to cross a union picket line,” the new lawmakers wrote. “From our understanding, thousands of UAW members who belong to the Harvard Graduate Students Union (HGSU-UAW Local 5118) are on strike, seeking basic provisions like a cost of living increase. In addition, thousands of members of the Harvard Academic Workers (HAW-UAW) have been bargaining for a first contract for over two years and recently went on a week-long strike.

“While we appreciate the invitation to Harvard’s Institute of Politics, we will not cross a picket line. So long as these workers are on strike, any trip we take to Harvard would be to stand in solidarity with our striking union siblings,” they added.
Three of the new House members, Sam Forstag of Montana, Clare Valdez of New York and Bob Brooks of Pennsylvania, posted a social media video statement in support of the striking workers.

“ For some of those workers at Harvard, it’s been more than two years since they organized that they have been fighting just to get a contract with basic protections against harassment at the workplace, basic discrimination protections and a cost of living raise to $50,000 a year,” Forstag said in the video. “Harvard has an endowment of $68 billion; they can afford to pay people a living wage. Our brothers and sisters there deserve a fair contract.

“So to all the workers at Harvard, we’ve got your back,” he added. “And to the administration at Harvard, well, if me and so many other members of Congress are going to be making a trip out there in December, it’s going to be to join our brothers and sisters on the picket line.”

“This freshman class stands with the working class,” Valdez added in a social media post . “Solidarity to my @UAW @hgsuuaw siblings at Harvard who are holding the line for what every worker deserves: living wages, workplace protections, and dignity on the job.”

In a post on X, incoming Democrat Richard Ojeda of North Carolina wrote: “I’ll never cross a picket line. You can find me shoulder to shoulder in solidarity fighting the good fight with our union siblings, full stop.”
The incoming Democrats are part of the largest freshman class in the US House in three decades. In January, more than 100 new members will be sworn into Congress’s lower chamber.
body_zh: 53名即将上任的众议院民主党人抵制哈佛迎新活动，支持研究生罢工|哈佛大学
民主党人说，我们被告知，要参加你们的活动，我们将被要求跨越工会纠察线。
周二，53 名新当选的国会议员告诉哈佛大学，他们将抵制下个月在哈佛大学肯尼迪学院举行的非正式迎新活动，以支持该校罢工的研究生联盟。
在给大学管理人员的一封信中，即将上任的众议院民主党人对邀请参加新当选国会议员两党计划表示感谢，自 1972 年以来已有 800 多名议员参加了该计划。
新立法者写道：“尽管我们很想参加，但我们被告知，要参加你们的活动，我们将被要求跨越工会纠察线。” “据我们了解，哈佛研究生会 (HGSU-UAW Local 5118) 的数千名 UAW 成员正在罢工，寻求提高生活费用等基本条款。此外，哈佛学术工作者 (HAW-UAW) 的数千名成员已经为第一份合同讨价还价了两年多，最近举行了为期一周的罢工。
他们补充说：“虽然我们感谢哈佛大学政治学院的邀请，但我们不会跨越纠察线。只要这些工人还在罢工，我们去哈佛的任何一次旅行都将与我们罢工的工会兄弟姐妹站在一起。”
三名新众议院议员——蒙大拿州的萨姆·福斯塔格、纽约州的克莱尔·瓦尔迪兹和宾夕法尼亚州的鲍勃·布鲁克斯——发布了社交媒体视频声明，支持罢工工人。
福斯塔格在视频中表示：“对于哈佛的一些员工来说，他们组织起来已经两年多了，他们一直在努力争取一份合同，其中包含基本的工作场所骚扰保护、基本的歧视保护以及生活费用提高到每年 5 万美元。” “哈佛拥有 680 亿美元的捐赠基金；他们有能力向人们支付生活工资。我们那里的兄弟姐妹应该得到一份公平的合同。
“所以对于哈佛的所有工作人员，我们会支持你们，”他补充道。 “对于哈佛政府来说，如果我和许多其他国会议员要在 12 月前往那里，那将是与我们的兄弟姐妹一起参加纠察线。”
“这个新生班级与工人阶级站在一起，”瓦尔迪兹在社交媒体帖子中补充道。 “声援我在哈佛的@UAW @hgsuuaw 兄弟姐妹，他们坚守阵线，争取每个工人应得的权利：生活工资、工作场所保护和工作尊严。”
北卡罗来纳州即将上任的民主党议员理查德·奥赫达（Richard Ojeda）在X上发帖写道：“我永远不会越过罢工警戒线。你们会看到我与工会兄弟姐妹们肩并肩、团结一心，为正义事业而战，绝无例外。”
即将上任的民主党人是三十年来美国众议院最大的新生阶层的一部分。一月份，100 多名新议员将宣誓进入国会下议院。

body_en: US inflation hits highest since May after prices climb 3.8% over the last year | US economy
Rise occurs amid soaring energy prices, according to last inflation reading before a crucial Fed board meeting
The sell-off in US tech stocks continued on Wednesday as investors reacted to continued concern over the AI trade and fresh data that showed inflation jumped in October.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq index was down over 4% on Wednesday morning, while the S&P 500 had lost over 2.5% and the Dow had dropped about 2%. By the end of the day the tech-heavy index was down 0.6%, the S&P had lost 0.25% and the Dow managed a small gain of 0.33%.
After a rally upon the return of CEO Jensen Huang, Nvidia was down 5% at market’s closing on Tuesday and fell another 4% on Wednesday.
High prices force many across the US to scale back for Thanksgiving: ‘We can’t afford the food’
Anthropic shares rose 1% to end the day at $82.79, marginally lower than the $83-a-share price it was listed for during its blockbuster IPO last week.
New data released on Wednesday had shown consumer prices rose an annualized 3.8% in October, the highest rate since May.

This is the last inflation reading before a crucial US Federal Reserve board meeting next month, in which officials are largely expected to hike interest rates for the second time this year. The Fed has set a target inflation rate of 2%, a level not seen since February 2021. Higher interest rates make it more expensive to borrow money, slowing price increases, and raising the price of loans like mortgages and student debt.

Prices rose 0.3% from September to October amid soaring energy prices, according to the personal consumption expenditure index, the Fed’s preferred inflation measure from the commerce department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis.
The data comes after the Bureau of Labor Statistics separately reported prices climbed 0.4% from September to October, higher than economists had anticipated.
Energy prices, including gas prices at the pump, have cooled, going from a high of $4.41 a gallon in early October to $3.61 a gallon by mid-November, according to AAA .
Though Fed officials held rates steady at the last board meeting in late October, minutes from the meeting showed that some expressed concern about inflation’s stickiness.
“A few of them warned that further delay risked allowing high inflation to become entrenched or necessitating a larger and more disruptive tightening later,” the minutes said.

The move would come at a tumultuous time for the US economy. A new survey from the Conference Board released on Tuesday showed consumer confidence had ticked up in November to its highest level since January 2025, probably driven by the shake-up from the midterm elections .

At the same time, US stocks have been fluctuating from a mixture of uncertainty over datacenter regulations, continuing scandals coming out of Nvidia , and overall investor concern about the seemingly limitless amount of money being spent on building AI and the infrastructure to support it.
body_zh: 美国通胀创5月以来新高，物价较去年上涨3.8%美国经济
根据美联储重要会议之前的最新通胀数据，能源价格飙升之际出现上涨
由于投资者对人工智能交易的持续担忧以及显示 10 月份通胀飙升的新数据做出反应，美国科技股的抛售仍在继续。
以科技股为主的纳斯达克指数周三上午下跌超过 4%，而标准普尔 500 指数下跌超过 2.5%，道指下跌约 2%。截至收盘，科技股指数下跌 0.6%，标准普尔指数下跌 0.25%，道指小幅上涨 0.33%。
首席执行官黄仁勋回归后，英伟达股价上涨，周二收盘时下跌 5%，周三又下跌 4%。
高物价迫使美国许多人在感恩节缩减开支：“我们买不起食物”
Anthropic 股价当天上涨 1%，收于 82.79 美元，略低于上周其大规模 IPO 期间每股 83 美元的价格。
周三公布的新数据显示，10 月份消费者价格年率上涨 3.8%，为 5 月份以来的最高增幅。
这是下个月重要的美联储理事会会议之前的最后一次通胀数据，人们普遍预计官员们将在这次会议上进行今年第二次加息。美联储设定了 2% 的目标通胀率，这是自 2021 年 2 月以来的最高水平。利率上升使得借贷成本更高，减缓了物价上涨，并提高了抵押贷款和学生债务等贷款的价格。
根据美国商务部经济分析局美联储首选的通胀指标个人消费支出指数，由于能源价格飙升，9月至10月物价上涨了0.3%。
该数据发布之前，美国劳工统计局单独报告称，9 月至 10 月价格上涨 0.4%，高于经济学家的预期。
根据 AAA 的数据，包括加油站天然气价格在内的能源价格已经降温，从 10 月初的每加仑 4.41 美元的高位降至 11 月中旬的每加仑 3.61 美元。
尽管美联储官员在十月底的最后一次董事会会议上维持利率不变，但会议纪要显示，一些人对通胀的粘性表示担忧。
会议纪要称，“他们中的一些人警告称，进一步拖延可能会导致高通胀根深蒂固，或者需要稍后实施更大规模、更具破坏性的紧缩政策。”
此举正值美国经济动荡时期。世界大型企业联合会周二发布的一项新调查显示，11 月消费者信心指数升至 2025 年 1 月以来的最高水平，这可能是受到中期选​​举的影响。
与此同时，美国股市一直在波动，原因包括数据中心法规的不确定性、英伟达不断爆出的丑闻，以及投资者对看似无限的资金用于构建人工智能及其支持基础设施的担忧。

title_en: Army detonates toxic explosives at Iowa plant despite concerns
title_zh: 尽管存在担忧，军队还是在爱荷华州工厂引爆了有毒炸药
summary: The U.S. Army detonated a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday, after days of back-and-forth between politicians and the courts.
summary_zh: 经过政界人士数日的反复争执后，美国陆军周三在爱荷华州的一家军工厂引爆了一堆可降解的爆炸物。
body_en: The U.S. Army detonated a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday morning, following community outcry and a legal fight over concerns of a possible dust plume containing toxic lead particles spreading after the blast.

Five tons of unstable explosive material, containing the highly sensitive compound lead azide , were blown up in a controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, which is a small community of about 350 people, located four hours west of Chicago by car.

As scheduled, the detonation took place at 9 a.m. local time. A few loud pops rang out in livestream footage of the explosion published by The Associated Press, followed by a faint smoke cloud that rose up above the rooftop of the Armed Forces Reserve Center building that separated its cameras from the detonation site.

Fifteen minutes after it happened, the Environmental Protection Agency reported that zero lead was detected in the air by four monitoring stations in the area. Those sensors continued to show the same readings two hours later, according to the EPA.

The Army said in a follow-up social media post Wednesday evening that the Federal Emergency Management Agency had given an "all clear" around the plant. The Army also added that maps from the Pentagon's Defense Threat Reduction Agency indicated "ZERO airborne lead detection" from the detonation. FEMA said in a separate statement Wednesday night that its air monitoring results indicated there was "no detectable lead."
Army Maj. Gen. Eric P. Shirley, the commander of the operation, described the detonation as "tremendously successful" at a news conference Wednesday.

"I believe absolutely that we reduced, as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and the safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa," he said.

Rob Cekada, the director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, added that the operation went "100% as planned," with the blast driving the explosion into the ground and minimizing the amount of lead dispersed into the atmosphere, as designed.
"The explosion exceeded all expectations," a senior administration official told CBS News. "Maximum mitigation efforts achieved."

President Trump echoed that assessment in a social media post after the detonation, writing that "early reports from Iowa are that the Army's mitigation efforts have far exceeded expectations." An Army official told CBS News the detonation went "much better than projected," while current Iowa Gov. Kim Reynolds called it "successful."

"We remain in close contact with authorities on the ground, while state agencies continue to monitor incoming data from the State Emergency Operations Center," Reynolds said. "We will keep Iowans informed as details become available."

The Middletown plant housed about 68 barrels or roughly 10,000 pounds of lead azide, which has been used in ammunition since World War I. According to the Environmental Protection Agency , the explosives degraded over about 20 years in storage, giving way to a process called recrystallization that made the material more susceptible to accidental detonation from friction or other movement.

The Army had pushed to carry out the controlled detonation because of the public safety risks associated with the cache possibly blowing up on its own. But environmental groups and local residents attempted to block its plans, fearing the health and agricultural consequences of a toxic plume of lead dust that could disperse across the region after the blast.

The Army said it had taken steps to barricade the concrete bunkers holding the munitions and absorb the toxic dust, including with aqueous foam, which is used to extinguish fuel fires, environmental officials have said.

"Precise deployment of aqueous foam blocks, two walls of four 16,000-gallon water tanks, and gel blocks adjacent to the bunkers will absorb thermal energy and reduce airborne particulate emissions directly at the blast source," the Army said in a statement .
Officials had warned that a plume could spread over parts of southeastern Iowa and northeastern Missouri , potentially threatening homes, playgrounds, farmlands and other spaces.
Missouri Gov. Mike Kehoe said after the explosion that reports from federal and state officials in Iowa indicated it was "well-contained."

"Initial analysis shared with us by federal partners and Iowa Homeland Security and Emergency Management indicates that the mitigation measures appear to have been successful and the explosion was well-contained," Kehoe said on social media.

The detonation was postponed last week after environmental groups filed a lawsuit challenging the emergency permit the EPA had granted the Army to authorize it. The groups argued the agency had not provided residents of the area with adequate notice of its plans or evidence showing the detonation was the best course of action from a health and safety perspective.

But the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals' initial ruling blocking the detonation was lifted Monday . The court acknowledged "the very real risks presented by the Army's planned detonation," but ultimately found the risk of an uncontrolled explosion more harmful.
body_zh: 周三上午，美国陆军在爱荷华州一家军火工厂引爆了一堆可降解的爆炸物，此前社区对此表示强烈抗议，并就爆炸后可能含有有毒铅颗粒的尘埃蔓延的担忧展开了法律斗争。
位于米德尔敦的爱荷华州陆军弹药厂在受控爆炸中炸毁了五吨不稳定的爆炸材料，其中含有高度敏感的化合物叠氮化铅。米德尔敦是一个约有 350 人的小社区，位于芝加哥以西 4 小时车程处。
按照计划，爆炸于当地时间上午 9 点发生。美联社发布的爆炸现场直播片段中传出几声巨响，随后，武装部队预备役中心大楼的屋顶升起微弱的烟云，将摄像机与爆炸现场隔开。
事件发生十五分钟后，环境保护局报告称，该地区四个监测站检测到空气中铅含量为零。据美国环保局称，两小时后，这些传感器继续显示相同的读数。
陆军在周三晚间的后续社交媒体帖子中表示，联邦紧急事务管理局已对该工厂周围进行了“解除警报”。陆军还补充说，五角大楼国防威胁降低局的地图显示，爆炸中“机载铅检测为零”。联邦应急管理局周三晚上在另一份声明中表示，其空气监测结果表明“没有检测到铅”。
这次行动的指挥官、陆军少将埃里克·P·雪利在周三的新闻发布会上称这次爆炸“非常成功”。
他说：“我绝对相信，我们已经将米德尔敦人民和爱荷华州广大社区的健康和安全风险降低到接近零。”
酒精、烟草、枪械和爆炸物局局长罗布·塞卡达补充说，这次行动“100%按计划进行”，按照设计，爆炸将爆炸推入地下，并最大限度地减少了散布到大气中的铅量。
“爆炸超出了所有人的预期，”一名高级政府官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻。 “已实现最大程度的缓解努力。”
爆炸发生后，特朗普总统在社交媒体帖子中回应了这一评估，他写道，“爱荷华州的早期报告显示，陆军的缓解努力远远超出了预期。”一名陆军官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，爆炸“比预计的要好得多”，而现任爱荷华州州长金·雷诺兹则称其“成功”。
雷诺兹说：“我们与当地当局保持密切联系，同时州机构继续监控来自州紧急行动中心的传入数据。” “一旦获得详细信息，我们将随时向爱荷华州通报情况。”
米德尔敦工厂储存了约 68 桶（约 10,000 磅）叠氮化铅，自第一次世界大战以来，叠氮化铅一直被用于制造弹药。根据环境保护局的说法，这些炸药在储存了大约 20 年的时间里发生了降解，发生了一种称为“再结晶”的过程，使这种材料更容易因摩擦或其他运动而意外爆炸。
陆军之所以推动实施受控爆炸，是因为该藏品可能会自行爆炸，从而带来公共安全风险。但环保组织和当地居民试图阻止其计划，担心爆炸后有毒铅尘可能在整个地区扩散，对健康和农业造成影响。
环境官员表示，陆军表示已采取措施封锁存放弹药的混凝土掩体，并吸收有毒粉尘，包括使用水泡沫来扑灭燃料火灾。
陆军在一份声明中表示：“精确部署水性泡沫块、四个 16,000 加仑水箱的两壁以及邻近掩体的凝胶块将吸收热能并直接减少爆炸源处的空气颗粒物排放。”
官员们警告说，羽流可能会蔓延到爱荷华州东南部和密苏里州东北部的部分地区，可能威胁到房屋、游乐场、农田和其他空间。
密苏里州州长迈克·基霍（Mike Kehoe）在爆炸发生后表示，爱荷华州联邦和州官员的报告表明爆炸“得到了很好的控制”。
基霍在社交媒体上表示：“联邦合作伙伴和爱荷华州国土安全和应急管理部门与我们分享的初步分析表明，缓解措施似乎取得了成功，爆炸得到了很好的控制。”
上周，环保组织提起诉讼，质疑美国环保署授予陆军的紧急许可证，导致爆炸被推迟。这些团体认为，该机构没有向该地区的居民提供有关其计划的充分通知，也没有证据表明从健康和安全的角度来看，爆炸是最好的行动方案。
但第八巡回上诉法院阻止爆炸的初步裁决于周一被撤销。法院承认“陆军计划的爆炸带来了非常现实的风险”，但最终发现失控爆炸的风险更具危害性。

title_en: Maps show where Thanksgiving storms could disrupt holiday
title_zh: 地图显示感恩节风暴可能会扰乱假期
summary: Rain, snow and powerful winds were forecast to impact large stretches of the country on Thanksgiving, potentially disrupting holiday festivities and, in some areas, hampering travel plans.
summary_zh: 预计感恩节期间，雨、雪和强风将影响该国大片地区，可能会扰乱节日庆祝活动，
body_en: Maps show where Thanksgiving storms could impact holiday festivities, disrupt travel plans - CBS News

Various types of severe weather are expected to impact large stretches of the United States this week, potentially disrupting Thanksgiving plans and hampering travel for Americans along both coasts and into the middle of the country.

A storm developing Wednesday over Florida threatened to bring flooding to southeastern states before quickly traveling up the coast and moving into the Northeast in time for Thanksgiving. Forecasts showed the storm could generate high winds and heavy rain across the region, while areas in the Midwest, including St. Louis, could see snow around the holiday.

In New York City, organizers of the iconic Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade announced the parade is being postponed until Saturday due to the coming storm. It's the first time in the parade's 100-year history that it's been postponed, although it was not held at all from 1942 to 1944 because of World War II. In 1971, the balloons were grounded due to strong winds, but the parade still went on.
While the city isn't expected to get excessive rain, a relatively rare High Wind Warning was issued, and wind gusts could reach 60 mph.
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul on Wednesday night declared a state of emergency for New York City, along with Nassau, Suffolk and Westchester counties.
"We're expecting heavy rain and strong winds that could create dangerous travel conditions," she wrote on social media.
And in a travel advisory, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that forecasts showed the worst of the storm would likely hit the city beginning Thursday afternoon into the late Thursday night.

More than 80 million people were under alerts Wednesday as the National Weather Service warned of powerful wind gusts, potentially as intense as 70 mph, that could impact a massive stretch of the East Coast, from South Carolina up to Massachusetts.

In addition to New York, other major cities like Boston , Philadelphia and Washington, D.C., would likely receive chilly rainfall on Thanksgiving, but forecasters expected most metropolitan hubs to be spared from the highest amounts. The weather service did note a flash-flooding threat impacting the Southeast on Wednesday could shift toward New York City by Thursday.

Up to 5 inches of rain could fall in other places, especially in southeastern states like Florida and the Carolinas. As the storm continues to develop, those areas could also face damaging winds, tornadoes and, potentially, waterspouts, forecasters said. The storm system already brought more than half a foot of rain to Miami, causing flooding in South Florida.

Interior portions of the eastern U.S. and some spots in the Midwest could receive their first measurable snowfall of the season around Thanksgiving. The weather service issued several winter storm warnings and winter weather advisories for parts of Illinois and Missouri, including St. Louis, through Thursday evening, as sections of both states brace for up to 6 inches, or even 9 inches in certain areas, of snow.

"Roads, especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. The weight of snow on tree limbs may down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages," the weather service in St. Louis wrote in a Wednesday advisory , which recommended that people delay travel completely, if possible.

预计本周各种恶劣天气将影响美国大片地区，可能会扰乱感恩节计划，并阻碍美国人沿海岸线和进入美国中部的旅行。
周三佛罗里达州上空发生的一场风暴可能会给东南部各州带来洪水，然后迅速沿着海岸移动，并在感恩节前及时进入东北部。天气预报显示，风暴可能会在整个地区产生大风和大雨，而包括圣路易斯在内的中西部地区可能会在假期期间出现降雪。
在纽约市，标志性的梅西百货感恩节游行的组织者宣布，由于即将到来的暴风雨，游行将推迟到周六。尽管1942年至1944年由于第二次世界大战而根本没有举行，但这是阅兵式100年历史上第一次被推迟。 1971年，气球因强风搁浅，但游行仍在继续。
虽然预计该市不会出现过多降雨，但发布了相对罕见的大风警告，阵风速度可能达到 60 英里/小时。
纽约州州长凯西·霍赫尔周三晚间宣布纽约市以及拿骚、萨福克和韦斯特切斯特县进入紧急状态。
她在社交媒体上写道：“我们预计会有大雨和强风，这可能会造成危险的旅行条件。”
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 在一份旅行咨询中表示，预测显示，最严重的风暴可能会从周四下午到周四深夜袭击该市。
周三，超过 8000 万人处于警报状态，国家气象局警告说，强风可能会达到每小时 70 英里，可能会影响从南卡罗来纳州到马萨诸塞州的东海岸大片地区。
除纽约外，波士顿、费城和华盛顿特区等其他主要城市可能会在感恩节遭遇寒冷的降雨，但预报员预计大多数大都市中心都不会遭受最高降雨量的影响。气象部门确实注意到，周三影响东南部的山洪威胁可能会在周四转移到纽约市。
其他地方的降雨量可能高达 5 英寸，尤其是佛罗里达州和卡罗来纳州等东南部各州。预报员表示，随着风暴继续发展，这些地区还可能面临破坏性的大风、龙卷风，甚至可能出现水龙卷。风暴系统已经给迈阿密带来了超过半英尺的降雨，导致南佛罗里达州发生洪水。
美国东部内陆地区和中西部的一些地区可能会在感恩节前后迎来本季第一场可测量的降雪。截至周四晚上，气象局向伊利诺伊州和密苏里州部分地区（包括圣路易斯）发布了多项冬季风暴警报和冬季天气报告，这两个州的部分地区可能会出现高达 6 英寸的降雪，某些地区甚至有 9 英寸的降雪。
圣路易斯气象部门在周三的一份咨询报告中写道：“道路，尤其是桥梁和立交桥，可能会变得光滑且危险。树枝上的积雪可能会压垮电线，并可能导致零星断电。”该报告建议人们如果可能的话，完全推迟出行。

title_en: Trump prepares new round of tariffs on China, other U.S. trading partners
title_zh: 特朗普准备对中国和其他美国贸易伙伴征收新一轮关税
summary: The Trump administration proposed a new round of tariffs targeting China, the European Union and 12 other economies over policies it says have created excess industrial capacity. Why it matters: Trump officials are pressing ahead with his trade agenda despite
summary_zh: 特朗普政府提议对中国、欧盟和其他 12 个经济体征收新一轮关税，理由是其所制定的政策
body_en: The Trump administration proposed a new round of tariffs targeting China, the European Union and 12 other economies over policies it says have created excess industrial capacity.
Why it matters: Trump officials are pressing ahead with his trade agenda despite a Democratic midterm sweep fueled by affordability concerns.
Post-election polling indicates voters overwhelmingly want tariffs to stay at current levels or decline. There's relatively little support — even among Trump's base — for them rising.
Driving the news: The tariffs are the result of a trade investigation that launched in March
The proposed tariffs largely target specific goods, a narrower approach than the sweeping import levies the administration has previously imposed.
China is the exception: The proposed 20% tariff would apply to most Chinese imports, with that rate calibrated to preserve the nations' trade truce.
These new tariffs would not be added to existing ones aimed at combating forced labor or certain sector-specific tariffs, a senior U.S. official said.
The official added that the rate could rise to 40% if trade talks break down or China fails to live up to its commitments.
Between the lines: The proposed tariff rates for other major trading partners are consistent with parameters set out in trade deals, the official said.
Trade deals struck with the EU, Japan and South Korea last year established 15% tariff rates on most goods.
Other economies targeted include Taiwan, India, Indonesia and Vietnam.
On average, the proposals would raise existing tariff rates on targeted trading partners by roughly 5 percentage points, the official estimated.

The big picture: The investigation was conducted under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The administration contends that foreign industrial policies encourage companies to produce more goods than global demand can absorb, undercutting U.S. manufacturers.
The proposed tariffs are subject to a public comment period and hearings, with the levies taking effect as early as January, the official said.

What they're saying: In response to reports of the proposed tariffs , China dismissed U.S. claims of industrial overcapacity as a "false proposition" and urged Washington to preserve stable trade relations.
The prospect of renewed tariffs weighed on global stocks, particularly Asian markets, overnight.
U.S. futures were sharply lower early Wednesday as well.

Of note: The U.S. is also proposing tougher trade measures against Brazil, after imposing 25% tariffs in July over alleged unfair trade practices amid tensions between Trump and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
The administration proposes raising tariffs on sugar imports exceeding existing quotas (regardless of origin) and imposing a 10% levy on previously exempt Brazilian aircraft, a U.S. official said.
The bottom line: Trump's tariff agenda is moving forward as Democrats in the incoming Congress look to curb presidential authority over trade policy and lower Americans' costs .
body_zh: 特朗普政府提议对中国、欧盟和其他 12 个经济体征收新一轮关税，称其政策造成了工业产能过剩。
为什么重要：尽管民主党因负担能力担忧而在中期选举中大获全胜，但特朗普官员仍在推进他的贸易议程。
选举后的民意调查显示，绝大多数选民希望关税保持在当前水平或下降。即使在特朗普的支持者中，对他们崛起的支持也相对较少。
推动新闻：关税是三月份启动的贸易调查的结果
拟议的关税主要针对特定​​商品，比政府此前征收的全面进口税的范围更窄。
中国是个例外：提议的 20% 关税将适用于大多数中国进口产品，该税率经过调整以维持两国的贸易休战。
一位美国高级官员表示，这些新关税不会添加到旨在打击强迫劳动或某些特定行业的现有关税中。
该官员补充说，如果贸易谈判破裂或中国未能履行其承诺，税率可能升至 40%。
言外之意是：该官员表示，其他主要贸易伙伴的拟议关税税率与贸易协议中规定的参数一致。
去年与欧盟、日本和韩国达成的贸易协议规定对大多数商品征收 15% 的关税。
其他目标经济体包括台湾、印度、印度尼西亚和越南。
该官员估计，平均而言，这些提案将使目标贸易伙伴的现有关税税率提高约 5 个百分点。
总体情况：调查是根据 1974 年《贸易法》第 301 条进行的。政府认为，外国产业政策鼓励企业生产超出全球需求所能吸收的商品，从而削弱了美国制造商的利益。
这位官员表示，拟议的关税将接受公众意见征询期和听证会，最早将于一月份生效。
他们的言论：针对拟议关税的报道，中国驳斥了美国关于工业产能过剩的说法，称其为“错误主张”，并敦促华盛顿保持稳定的贸易关系。
隔夜，新关税的前景令全球股市，尤其是亚洲市场承压。
周三早些时候美国期货也大幅走低。
值得注意的是：在特朗普与巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦之间关系紧张之际，美国7月因涉嫌不公平贸易行为而对巴西征收25%的关税，随后美国还提议对巴西采取更严厉的贸易措施。
一位美国官员表示，美国政府提议对超过现有配额（无论原产地）的食糖进口提高关税，并对之前豁免的巴西飞机征收 10% 的关税。
底线是：特朗普的关税议程正在向前推进，即将上任的国会中的民主党人希望限制总统在贸易政策上的权威并降低美国人的成本。

title_en: Judge temporarily blocks FCC from reviewing ABC's licenses
title_zh: 法官暂时阻止 FCC 审查 ABC 的许可证
summary: A federal judge blocked the FCC from moving forward with an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, a move the network argues is an attempt by the Trump administration to punish speech it does not like.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官阻止 FCC 对 ABC 的广播许可证进行早期审查，该网络认为此举是 T 部的一次尝试。
body_en: Judge temporarily blocks FCC from reviewing ABC's licenses after network alleged retaliation by Trump - CBS News

A federal judge blocked the Federal Communications Commission from moving forward with an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses Wednesday, a move the network argues is an attempt by the Trump administration to punish speech it does not like.

In a 45-page ruling, U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan found ABC is likely to succeed in showing the FCC's license review was retaliatory. Her preliminary injunction bars the FCC from "taking any continuing or further action against [ABC] in relation to the early license renewal proceedings" while the network's lawsuit against the agency works its way through the courts.

The judge pointed to at least 11 different examples of President Trump publicly urging the FCC to strip ABC of its licenses in recent years — an action the president argues is necessary because the network's news coverage or late-night shows are unfair to him.
AliKhan also said FCC Chair Brendan Carr — who frequently echoes Mr. Trump's criticism of media outlets — "has taken President Trump's rhetoric as his marching orders."

"Given the extreme, indeed existential, nature of the possible penalty Plaintiffs face—loss of their broadcast licenses—the court concludes that early license renewal proceedings create a risk sufficient to chill a broadcaster of ordinary firmness," the judge wrote.

She said the question of whether ABC's interest in a preliminary injunction outweighed the federal government's interests was "not a close case." She did not agree to ABC's request for a broader ban on "taking any actions, formal or informal, to coerce or threaten Plaintiffs with sanctions in an effort to alter their exercise of editorial discretion."
An ABC News spokesperson said: "Today's decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration."

An FCC spokesperson called the decision to grant ABC's motion "wrong on the facts and wrong on the law—as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear," and said the agency "looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter."

Earlier this year, the FCC ordered ABC to file early license renewal applications for the eight local television stations it owns and operates, saying it was investigating "possible violations" of the Communications Act of 1934 and the agency's prohibition on unlawful discrimination. The licenses originally weren't scheduled for renewal until 2028 to 2031.
ABC sued over the move , calling it "blatant retaliation" in violation of the First Amendment and arguing the FCC's investigation into discrimination was a pretext.

"Each day, Plaintiffs (and every other broadcaster observing the Commission's actions) face a choice between exercising independent editorial judgment or risking the loss of valuable broadcast licenses—precisely the type of choice that chills protected First Amendment activity and cannot be remedied after the fact," the network and Disney wrote in a filing.

At one point during a court hearing last month, Disney attorney Beth Wilkinson invoked the French Revolution, saying the FCC's review was forcing the company to sit with its "head on a guillotine" while it awaits a decision about the licenses.

The FCC has denied that it is seeking to punish ABC for its speech. Government lawyers say the agency has been investigating the broadcaster since last year over its compliance with anti-employment discrimination rules, alleging its responses to requests for information have been insufficient, leading the FCC to push for early license renewal.

"The commission decided to look for information that it needed by calling for early renewal of plaintiffs' broadcast license," Justice Department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remme said in last month's court hearing before AliKhan.

AliKhan appeared skeptical of the government's arguments in Wednesday's ruling. At one point, she noted that the FCC took action shortly after late-night ABC host Jimmy Kimmel joked that first lady Melania Trump had "the glow of an expectant widow."
She said "it is no coincidence that President Trump criticized Mr. Kimmel's skit on social media and the very next day Defendants initiated the early license renewal proceedings."

The Trump administration has often tangled with ABC and other outlets. Last year, following another controversial joke by Kimmel, Carr did not rule out punishing the network, saying on a podcast : "We can do this the easy way or the hard way."

More broadly, Carr has suggested networks could lose their licenses for coverage of the Iran war, and Mr. Trump called for licenses to be revoked when some networks opted out of carrying a primetime speech in July. The FCC has also warned daytime and late-night talk shows that they must provide equal time to political candidates — a rule that historically hasn't applied to them. Separately, the administration has sought to restrict some outlets' access to the White House.
Judge declines to issue long-term ban on tax-funded pro-Trump ads
body_zh: 在网络涉嫌特朗普报复后，法官暂时阻止 FCC 审查 ABC 的许可证 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
周三，一名联邦法官阻止联邦通信委员会对美国广播公司的广播许可证进行早期审查，该网络认为此举是特朗普政府试图惩罚其不喜欢的言论。
在一份长达 45 页的裁决中，美国地区法官 Loren AliKhan 认为 ABC 很可能成功证明 FCC 的许可审查是报复性的。她的初步禁令禁止联邦通信委员会“在早期许可证更新程序中针对 [ABC] 采取任何持续或进一步的行动”，而该网络针对该机构的诉讼正在通过法院进行。
法官指出，近年来特朗普总统公开敦促 FCC 吊销 ABC 的许可证至少有 11 个不同的例子，总统认为此举是必要的，因为该网络的新闻报道或深夜节目对他不公平。
阿里汗还表示，经常回应特朗普对媒体机构批评的联邦通信委员会主席布伦丹·卡尔“已将特朗普总统的言论视为他的前进命令”。
法官写道：“鉴于原告可能面临的惩罚的极端性，甚至是生死攸关的性质——失去广播许可证——法院的结论是，过早的许可证续签程序所造成的风险足以让一家普通的广播公司感到不寒而栗。”
她表示，关于美国广播公司对初步禁令的兴趣是否超过联邦政府的利益的问题“并不是一个悬而未决的案件”。她不同意美国广播公司的要求，即更广泛地禁止“采取任何正式或非正式的行动，通过制裁来胁迫或威胁原告，以改变他们行使编辑自由裁量权”。
美国广播公司新闻发言人表示：“今天的判决是第一修正案的重要胜利。我们感谢法院的认真考虑。”
FCC 的一位发言人称，批准 ABC 动议的决定“在事实上是错误的，在法律上也是错误的——最高法院的判例清楚地表明了这一点”，并表示该机构“期待在此事上取得全面胜利”。
今年早些时候，美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 要求美国广播公司 (ABC) 为其拥有和运营的八家地方电视台提前提交许可证更新申请，称其正在调查“可能违反”1934 年《通信法》和该机构禁止非法歧视的规定。这些许可证最初计划在 2028 年至 2031 年之前更新。
ABC 对此举动提起诉讼，称其为违反第一修正案的“公然报复”，并辩称 FCC 对歧视的调查只是一个借口。
该网络和迪士尼在一份文件中写道：“每天，原告（以及所有其他观察委员会行为的广播公司）都面临着一个选择：是行使独立的编辑判断，还是冒着失去宝贵的广播许可证的风险——正是这种选择，使受保护的第一修正案活动感到寒心，而且事后无法补救。”
在上个月的法庭听证会上，迪士尼律师贝丝·威尔金森(Beth Wilkinson)一度援引法国大革命，称联邦通信委员会的审查迫使该公司在等待有关许可的决定时“将头放在断头台上”。
美国联邦通信委员会否认正在寻求惩罚美国广播公司的言论。政府律师表示，该机构自去年以来一直在调查该广播公司是否遵守反就业歧视规则，声称其对信息请求的回应不够充分，导致联邦通信委员会推动提前更新许可证。
司法部律师 Dimitar Georgiev-Remme 在阿里汗上个月的法庭听证会上表示：“委员会决定通过呼吁提前续签原告的广播许可证来寻找所需的信息。”
阿里汗似乎对政府在周三裁决中的论点持怀疑态度。她一度指出，美国广播公司深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔开玩笑说第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普“焕发着准寡妇的光芒”后不久，美国联邦通信委员会就采取了行动。
她说，“特朗普总统在社交媒体上批评金梅尔先生的短剧，第二天被告就启动了提前续签程序，这并非巧合。”
特朗普政府经常与美国广播公司和其他媒体发生争执。去年，在金梅尔提出另一个有争议的笑话后，卡尔不排除惩罚该网络的可能性，他在播客上说：“我们可以通过简单的方法或困难的方法来做到这一点。”
更广泛地说，卡尔表示电视网可能会失去报道伊朗战争的许可证，而当一些电视网选择不进行七月份的黄金时段演讲时，特朗普呼吁吊销许可证。美国联邦通信委员会还警告白天和深夜的脱口秀节目，它们必须为政治候选人提供平等的时间——这一规则历来没有适用于他们。另外，政府还试图限制一些媒体进入白宫。
