title_en: Trump takes credit for Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, says its good for the economy
title_zh: 特朗普将黄仁勋重返英伟达归功于他，称这对经济有利
summary: President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company -- and good for the United States economy.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统称赞黄仁勋重返英伟达高管，这对公司有利，对美国经济也有利。
body_en: Trump takes credit for Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia, says its good for the economy President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company -- and good for the United States economy.
President Trump touted the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia's C-suite as good for the company — and good for the United States economy.
Jensen Huang is back as CEO of Nvidia less than two weeks after resigning, a return that President Trump helped engineer and is now celebrating.

Huang and the president have been allies. His company donated to the new White House ballroom. Huang also routinely advised the president on AI policy. He will surely face questions about that relationship and much more when he attends a closed-door interview that three House committees have planned for next week. In a moment, we bring in Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, who's on two of those panels. We begin with the news.
MARTIN: White House correspondent Danielle Kurtzleben has been covering this. Good morning.
MARTIN: So what has the president had to say about his role in all of this Nvidia situation?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, shortly after the announcement of the reinstatement, the president posted that this was for the good not only of Nvidia, but the U.S. economy. And then yesterday morning, he did a 50-minute phone interview with CNBC. And Trump was asked if he directly called into the Nvidia board meeting, and he demurred, but he did make it clear that he pushed the company on this decision. He said he convinced them - his words. He went on to say that he was able to convince Nvidia because the company's stock had plummeted following Huang's ouster, and that was again after the news initially broke that Huang was having an affair with an alleged spy for China.

MARTIN: Now, let me just pause here because I'm not sure that - perhaps if people don't cover the business world, etc., they might not know that it is very extraordinary for a White House to weigh in on private business decisions.

KURTZLEBEN: Yeah. It's a huge deal. Even if it's not really unusual for this White House to intervene in the economy and even private businesses, this White House has taken stakes in dozens of companies, for example. Plus, Trump has gotten very cozy with the tech world, with CEOs showing up to White House events or donating to his ballroom. But beyond all that, it really stood out to me this thing that Trump did yesterday - he posted this meme playing off that famous picture of him after he was shot in Butler, Pennsylvania. In this new picture, it's Huang, not Trump, raising his fist with blood spattered on his face. And in that fist is a red bra, referencing, of course, Huang's affair. Now, this is the president of the United States posting this, and it's trolling. And also it's once again celebrating a private business decision.
MARTIN: Extraordinary. That image is extraordinary. But why was the president so dead set on getting Huang back into his CEO role?

KURTZLEBEN: Well, Trump told CNBC he was concerned that Chinese president Xi Jinping might lure Huang over to China to boost their chip business. But also let's remember Trump loves to talk about the stock market. Even when other economic measures aren't looking great, he often has stock indexes to talk about. So he told CNBC the Huang decision not only turned Nvidia's stock around, but maybe the whole market after what was a rough week for stocks.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: I watched the screen, and I said, boy, that thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taken the whole market with it.
UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: It's just an incredible turnaround.
UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: You've been watching corporate America...
TRUMP: There could be - it could be that there's never been anything like it, actually.

KURTZLEBEN: One other important point here - the president has been trading in Nvidia stock, as we know from his financial disclosures. In early September, there was a purchase he made worth up to a quarter of a million dollars. And this is also part of a pattern of trading in companies by the president that also are affected by his administration's actions.
MARTIN: OK. The national security issues. What is the status of that? It strikes me that those issues have not been resolved. Have they?
body_zh: 特朗普将黄仁勋重返英伟达视为功劳，称这对经济有利 特朗普总统称赞黄仁勋重返英伟达高管对公司有利，对美国经济也有利。
特朗普总统称赞黄仁勋重返英伟达高管，这对公司有利，对美国经济也有利。
黄仁勋在辞职不到两周后重新担任英伟达首席执行官，这是特朗普总统帮助策划的回归，现在正在庆祝。
黄和总统一直是盟友。他的公司向新的白宫宴会厅捐款。黄还经常就人工智能政策向总统提供建议。当他参加众议院三个委员会计划下周举行的闭门采访时，他肯定会面临有关这种关系以及更多问题的问题。一会儿，我们请来代表 Raja Krishnamoorthi，他是其中两个小组的成员。我们从新闻开始。
马丁：白宫记者丹妮尔·库茨莱本一直在报道此事。早上好。
马丁：那么对于他在 Nvidia 的所有事件中所扮演的角色，总统有什么想说的？

KURTZLEBEN：嗯，在宣布恢复后不久，总统表示这不仅有利于 Nvidia，也有利于美国经济。昨天早上，他接受了 CNBC 50 分钟的电话采访。当特朗普被问到他是否直接参加英伟达董事会会议时，他表示反对，但他确实明确表示，他推动该公司做出了这一决定。他说他说服了他们——他的话。他接着说，他之所以能够说服英伟达，是因为在黄仁勋被罢黜后，该公司的股价暴跌，而这又是在黄仁勋与一名所谓的中国间谍有染的消息最初传出之后。
马丁：现在，让我在这里暂停一下，因为我不确定 - 也许如果人们不报道商业世界等，他们可能不知道白宫参与私人商业决策是非常不寻常的。

库兹莱本：是的。这是一件大事。即使本届白宫干预经济甚至私营企业并不罕见，但例如，本届白宫已经入股了数十家公司。此外，特朗普与科技界变得非常融洽，首席执行官们出席白宫活动或向他的舞厅捐款。但除此之外，特朗普昨天做的这件事对我来说真的很突出——他发布了这个表情包，模仿了他在宾夕法尼亚州巴特勒被枪杀后的那张著名照片。在这张新照片中，是黄，而不是特朗普，举起了拳头，脸上溅满了血。拳头里有一个红色胸罩，当然是指黄的外遇。现在，这是美国总统发布的，这是恶搞。它还再次庆祝私营企业的决定。
马丁：非凡。那画面非同寻常。但为什么总统如此执意要让黄重新担任首席执行官一职呢？
KURTZLEBEN：嗯，特朗普告诉 CNBC，他担心中国国家主席习近平可能会引诱黄仁勋到中国来发展他们的芯片业务。但我们也要记住，特朗普喜欢谈论股市。即使其他经济指标看起来不太好，他也经常谈论股票指数。因此，他告诉 CNBC，黄仁勋的决定不仅扭转了英伟达股票的走势，而且可能扭转了整个市场在股市经历了艰难的一周后的走势。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：我看着屏幕，我说，天哪，那件事就像一艘朝错误方向行驶的火箭飞船。现在，它就像一艘火箭，正朝着正确的方向前进，并带动了整个市场。
身份不明的人：这真是一个令人难以置信的转变。
身份不明的人：您一直在关注美国企业界……
特朗普：可能有——实际上可能从来没有发生过这样的事情。
KURTZLEBEN：另一个重要的一点是，总统一直在交易 Nvidia 股票，正如我们从他的财务披露中了解到的那样。 9月初，他购买了一笔价值高达25万美元的商品。这也是总统公司交易模式的一部分，这些公司也受到其政府行为的影响。
马丁：好的。国家安全问题。其状态如何？令我震惊的是，这些问题还没有得到解决。他们有吗？

title_en: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
title_zh: 民主党人调查小特朗普的企业是否受益于政府准入
summary: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.
summary_zh: 调查人员表示，自小唐纳德·特朗普的父亲连任以来，与他的投资公司 1789 Capital 有联系的公司已经获利。
body_en: Donald Trump Jr. speaks on stage on the second day of the 2026 Republican National Convention on Sept. 10, in Dallas. Brandon Bell/Getty Images hide caption

Congressional Democrats, led by likely House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, are expanding their investigation into the investment firm 1789 Capital, which brought on Donald Trump Jr. as a partner days after his father's reelection to the White House.

Since then, investigators say the firm has grown from "a middling venture capital firm" with $150 million in managed assets to "the darling of the venture capital world" with $3 billion in managed assets.

Investigators want to determine whether the growth was boosted by the president's son leveraging political influence or government information to secure federal contracts and regulatory changes for companies with connections to the investment firm.
House Democrat warns 13 Trump allies to save their records for upcoming investigations

Trump Jr. told Axios last week that the timing of his hiring at 1789 Capital was coincidental, noting that he had already been working with founder Omeed Malik for years. He also said he draws a clear line when marketing and raising money for the firm.

"I make it very clear [to foreign investors] that I have nothing to do with government," Trump Jr. said. "[The president is] my father, but he's also busy and I probably haven't spoken to him in three weeks."

He also suggested he doesn't use or need government connections to make smart investments. "Trying to do the things that we're alleged to be doing every day, I think that would last for about two seconds before it was out there very publicly," Trump Jr. said. He added that the firm relies on teams of analysts to make investments in industries where there are obvious public and national security demands but relatively few companies who are able to meet those needs.
NPR reached out to Donald Trump Jr. for comment and did not hear back.

Regarding Raskin's request for documents from 1789 Capital, Bill Burck, an attorney representing the firm, told NPR, "We responded to Congressman Raskin back in September pointing out in detail the many flaws in his understanding of how 1789 has operated and a number of basic factual errors. He never bothered to reply. Facts are facts and Congressman Raskin has them wrong here but persists in his tall tales against 1789. These are personal attacks untethered to actual evidence."

On Monday, congressional investigators sent letters to four companies — military contractor Hadrian, electronic cigarette company Juul, prediction market Polymarket and online weapons dealer GrabAGun — asking them to preserve their records and turn over a broad array of records to the committee.

The committee is interested in Hadrian's contracts with the armed forces, signed in March of this year, worth close to a billion dollars. Investigators allege that, in 2024, the company had a single manufacturing facility and "no history of fulfilling government contracts." They also noted that CEO Chris Power donated tens of thousands of dollars to Trump-aligned political organizations in advance of the 2024 election.

Political donations are constitutionally-protected speech and not necessarily evidence of wrongdoing. 1789 Capital first invested in Hadrian in July 2025. The company is also backed by a number of bluechip investors, including Morgan Stanley, T. Rowe Price, Andreessen Horowitz and JPMorganChase. Hadrian did not reply to a request for comment from NPR.

Investigators also allege that Trump Jr.'s firm took a stake in e-cigarette company Juul in March 2025, as the company teetered near insolvency following rulings during the first Trump administration limiting the sale of various flavor cartridges. Four months after that investment, though before it was publicly disclosed, investigators say the company's fortunes rebounded after the Trump administration authorized five new Juul e-cigarette products. The company has announced plans for more flavor authorization applications moving forward.

In a statement to NPR, a Juul spokesperson said the company had received Rep. Raskin's letter and are "reviewing it closely. As always, we intend to cooperate with any Congressional effort to understand our company, our commitment to combating underage vaping, and our mission to help adult smokers of combustible cigarettes transition completely away from smoking."

Investigators are also interested in betting site Polymarket. They say that following a meeting between Polymarket leadership and Trump Jr. at the 2024 Republican National Convention, 1789 Capital invested in the company — which at the time was banned in the United States. In July 2025, after President Trump took office, the Justice Department and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission notified the company that they had closed investigations launched during the Biden administration, according to reporting from Bloomberg News. The CFTC later authorized a U.S. version of the platform to launch. Investigators allege 1789's investment resulted in a 70-fold return.
Donald Trump Jr.'s venture capital firm will be major financial backer of Polymarket

GrabAGun, a company that "believe[s] people should be able to use their computers, phones, and tablets to shop for firearms the same way they purchase everything else," became, according to investigators, a publicly-traded company with the help of 1789 Capital leadership, including Trump Jr., who serves of its board.

In May 2026, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) proposed a draft rule that would make it easier to ship guns directly to people's homes. At the time, GrabAGun claimed that the company is "uniquely positioned to capitalize on this potential opportunity." Investigators are seeking to understand what knowledge and involvement Trump Jr. had of the proposed rule change.
body_zh: 9 月 10 日，小唐纳德·特朗普在达拉斯举行的 2026 年共和党全国代表大会第二天上台发表讲话。布兰登·贝尔/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
由可能担任众议院司法委员会主席的马里兰州众议员杰米·拉斯金 (Jamie Raskin) 领导的国会民主党人正在扩大对投资公司 1789 Capital 的调查，该公司在小唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump Jr.) 父亲连任白宫几天后聘请了该公司作为合伙人。
调查人员表示，自那时起，该公司已从管理资产 1.5 亿美元的“中等风险投资公司”成长为管理资产 30 亿美元的“风险投资界宠儿”。
调查人员希望确定，总统之子利用政治影响力或政府信息来确保与该投资公司有联系的公司获得联邦合同和监管变化，从而推动了增长。
众议院民主党人警告特朗普的 13 名盟友保存他们的记录以供即将进行的调查
小特朗普上周告诉 Axios，他被 1789 Capital 聘用的时机很巧合，并指出他已经与创始人奥米德·马利克 (Omeed Malik) 合作多年。他还表示，他在为公司营销和筹集资金时划清了界限。
“我（向外国投资者）明确表示，我与政府没有任何关系，”小特朗普说。 “[总统是]我的父亲，但他也很忙，我可能已经三周没有和他说过话了。”
他还表示，他不会利用或不需要政府关系来进行明智的投资。小特朗普说：“我认为，我们试图做据称每天都在做的事情，这种情况会持续大约两秒钟，然后才会公开。”他补充说，该公司依靠分析师团队对存在明显公共和国家安全需求但能够满足这些需求的公司相对较少的行业进行投资。
美国国家公共广播电台联系小唐纳德·特朗普征求意见，但没有得到回复。
关于拉斯金要求 1789 Capital 提供文件的问题，代表该公司的律师比尔·伯克 (Bill Burck) 告诉 NPR，“我们在 9 月份回复了拉斯金国会议员，详细指出了他对 1789 运作方式的理解中的许多缺陷以及一些基本的事实错误。他从来没有费心回复。事实就是事实，拉斯金国会议员在这里错了，但仍然坚持他对 1789 的荒诞故事。这些都是人身攻击。”不受实际证据的束缚。”
周一，国会调查人员致函四家公司——军事承包商 Hadrian、电子烟公司 Juul、预测市场 Polymarket 和在线武器经销商 GrabAGun——要求他们保存记录并向委员会移交大量记录。
该委员会对哈德良与武装部队今年三月签署的价值近十亿美元的合同感兴趣。调查人员称，到 2024 年，该公司只有一个制造工厂，并且“没有履行政府合同的历史”。他们还指出，首席执行官克里斯·鲍尔 (Chris Power) 在 2024 年大选之前向特朗普结盟的政治组织捐赠了数万美元。
政治捐款是受宪法保护的言论，并不一定是不当行为的证据。 1789 Capital于2025年7月首次投资Hadrian。该公司还得到了多家蓝筹投资者的支持，包括摩根士丹利、T. Rowe Price、Andreessen Horowitz和摩根大通。哈德良没有回复 NPR 的置评请求。
调查人员还指控，小特朗普的公司于 2025 年 3 月入股了电子烟公司 Juul，因为在特朗普第一届政府期间做出限制各种口味烟弹销售的裁决后，该公司濒临破产。这项投资虽然尚未公开披露，但四个月后，调查人员表示，在特朗普政府批准五种新的 Juul 电子烟产品后，该公司的命运出现了反弹。该公司已宣布计划继续进行更多风味授权申请。
Juul 发言人在给 NPR 的一份声明中表示，该公司已收到众议员拉斯金的信函，并“正在仔细审查。一如既往，我们打算配合国会的任何努力，以了解我们公司、我们对打击未成年人吸电子烟的承诺，以及我们帮助成年吸烟者完全戒烟的使命。”

调查人员还对博彩网站 Polymarket 感兴趣。他们表示，在 Polymarket 领导层与小特朗普在 2024 年共和党全国代表大会上会面后，1789 Capital 投资了该公司——该公司当时在美国是被禁止的。据彭博社报道，2025 年 7 月，特朗普总统上任后，司法部和商品期货交易委员会通知该公司，他们已结束拜登政府期间发起的调查。美国商品期货交易委员会随后授权推出该平台的美国版本。调查人员称，1789 的投资带来了 70 倍的回报。
小唐纳德·特朗普的风险投资公司将成为 Polymarket 的主要财务支持者
GrabAGun 是一家“相信人们应该能够像购买其他东西一样使用电脑、手机和平板电脑购买枪支”的公司，据调查人员称，在 1789 Capital 领导层（包括担任其董事会成员的小特朗普）的帮助下，该公司成为了一家上市公司。
2026 年 5 月，烟酒枪械和爆炸物管理局 (ATF) 提出了一项规则草案，旨在让枪支直接运送到人们家中变得更加容易。当时，GrabAGun 声称该公司“处于独特的地位，可以利用这一潜在机会”。调查人员正在试图了解小特朗普对拟议的规则变更有哪些了解和参与。

title_en: A look at the probes involving Nvidia, Jensen Huang and Megaspeed
title_zh: 涉及 Nvidia、Jensen Huang 和 Megaspeed 的调查一览
summary: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and CEO of Nvidia sent shockwaves through the political and business world, and has fueled scrutiny by Congress.
summary_zh: 黄仁勋重新担任英伟达总裁兼首席执行官，在政界和商界引起了震动，并引发了各方的密切关注。
body_en: Washington — Revelations that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese intelligence asset have put the leading AI company under a microscope, as lawmakers and states question whether Nvidia skirted federal export rules that aim to stop its most advanced chips from going to China.

While Huang initially resigned his post amid scrutiny of his relationship with Alice Huang , a former executive at the Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, Nvidia's board of directors announced Monday that it reinstated Huang as president and CEO .

News of Huang's return to Nvidia sent shockwaves through the business and political worlds, even as President Trump said he had spoken to the board and "convinced them" to bring Huang back. The president told CNBC in an interview that his administration gave Nvidia "assurances" that Huang is not a threat to national security.

The company, meanwhile, said it received "input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."
Still, investigations by at least one state and Congress are unlikely to be derailed by Huang's dramatic return to Nvidia.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia last week following revelations of Huang's affair with the woman who is alleged to have ties to China's Ministry of State Security.

Bonta, a Democrat, said the state's Department of Justice is seeking information from Nvidia about whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether the company misled investors and the public.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," he said in a statement. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law."
Bonta said the information his office receives from Nvidia will help determine whether the company broke state law.

Numerous congressional committees were readying investigations into Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese spy, and his reinstatement as CEO did not diminish lawmakers' appetite for more information about Huang's actions and whether his company's chips were diverted to China.

Huang is set to answer questions behind closed doors from lawmakers on three House panels, the Intelligence, Foreign Affairs and China Select Committee, on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, will appear before the committees on Dec. 2.
The Senate Banking Committee will then hold a public hearing with Huang on Dec. 3.

Democrats, who will take control of the House and Senate in January, say they intend to launch investigations into Nvidia and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whose agency oversees government export controls on sensitive technology.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to serve as House speaker in the next Congress, denounced the decision by Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang as "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible."

"Congress will not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce," he said in a statement Monday.

"Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he's learned nothing from his resounding election defeat," Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer wrote on X. "Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain."

Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, who is poised to take the helm of the Senate Banking Committee in January, said Nvidia officials and the Trump administration will have to answer questions from lawmakers.

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," she said in a statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement."
House and Senate Democrats have also demanded that the president and his administration provide information about their role in Huang's reinstatement.

"President Trump has acknowledged personally intervening on Huang's behalf, and Nvidia has acknowledged that it received 'input from senior levels of the United States government' in reaching its decision," a group of five Democratic senators said in a joint statement. "The American people deserve to know why the president intervened in this extraordinary manner, whether serious counterintelligence or national security concerns were disregarded, and whose interests this intervention was intended to serve."
body_zh: 华盛顿——英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名据称是中国情报人员的女性发生婚外情的消息让这家领先的人工智能公司受到了密切关注，立法者和各州质疑英伟达是否规避了旨在阻止其最先进芯片进入中国的联邦出口规定。
虽然黄最初因与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 的关系受到审查而辞职，但英伟达董事会周一宣布恢复黄担任总裁兼首席执行官。
黄回到英伟达的消息在商界和政界引起了震动，尽管特朗普总统表示他已与董事会交谈并“说服他们”让黄回来。总统在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，他的政府向英伟达做出了“保证”，黄仁勋不会对国家安全构成威胁。
与此同时，该公司表示，它收到了“美国政府高层的意见，根据这些意见，董事会相信黄先生的复职不会构成国家安全风险。”
尽管如此，至少一个州和国会的调查不太可能因为黄仁勋戏剧性地重返英伟达而中断。
上周，黄与一名据称与中国国家安全部有联系的女子的婚外情被曝光后，加州总检察长罗布·邦塔 (Rob Bonta) 向英伟达发出了调查传票。
民主党人邦塔表示，该州司法部正在向英伟达寻求信息，了解其先进芯片或机密信息是否可能流向中国，以及该公司是否误导了投资者和公众。
他在一份声明中表示：“英伟达及其前首席执行官的行为发出了明亮的危险信号，包括该公司可能误导投资者的方式。” “我的办公室正在调查英伟达或黄仁勋的行为是否导致中国获得先进芯片或机密信息，以及英伟达是否在这一风险上误导了投资者和公众，从而违反了法律。”
邦塔表示，他的办公室从英伟达收到的信息将有助于确定该公司是否违反了州法律。
许多国会委员会正在准备调查黄与被指控的中国间谍的关系，而他重新担任首席执行官并没有减少立法者对黄的行为以及其公司的芯片是否被转移到中国的更多信息的兴趣。
黄仁勋将于 12 月 1 日在众议院三个小组（情报、外交事务和中国特别委员会）闭门回答议员提出的问题。Nvidia 的总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特 (Tim Teter) 将于 12 月 2 日出席这些委员会的听证会。
参议院银行委员会将于 12 月 3 日与黄先生举行公开听证会。
将于一月份控制参众两院的民主党人表示，他们打算对英伟达和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克展开调查，后者负责监督政府对敏感技术的出口管制。
预计将在下届国会担任众议院议长的众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 谴责英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋职务的决定是“站不住脚、不负责任且难以理解的”。
他在周一的一份声明中表示：“国会不会被阻止对 NVIDIA 的商业不法行为以及 Howard Lutnick 和商务部的腐败滥用权力行为进行迅速、彻底和广泛的调查。”
参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 在 X 上写道：“特朗普将自己的经济利益和亿万富翁伙伴的需求置于我们的国家安全之上，并强调他没有从选举惨败中吸取任何教训。民主党人将运用全部权力来调查特朗普政府、黄仁勋、其他 NVIDIA 高管以及任何为了经济利益而出卖我们国家安全的人的任何不当行为。”
马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 即将于 1 月份接任参议院银行委员会主席，她表示，英伟达官员和特朗普政府将必须回答立法者提出的问题。
她在一份声明中表示：“让黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官的鲁莽决定并没有改变这样一个事实：黄仁勋、NVIDIA 高管和公司董事会仍然需要国会就该公司遵守美国出口管制的情况做出答复。” “特朗普政府还需要向国会解释提供了哪些‘意见’，以及美国政府的哪些高级官员支持他的复职。”
众议院和参议院民主党人还要求总统和他的政府提供有关他们在黄的复职中所扮演的角色的信息。
五名民主党参议员在一份联合声明中表示：“特朗普总统承认亲自代表黄仁勋进行干预，英伟达也承认在做出决定时收到了‘美国政府高层的意见’。” “美国人民应该知道总统为何以这种非同寻常的方式进行干预，是否忽视了严重的反情报或国家安全问题，以及这种干预是为了服务谁的利益。”

title_en: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for 1st time in history
title_zh: 梅西百货感恩节大游行史上首次推迟
summary: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.
summary_zh: 梅西百货周三表示，梅西百货感恩节游行历史上首次因天气原因推迟。
body_en: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.
The 100th annual parade will now kick off Saturday at 8:30 a.m.
The historic move comes as a powerful coastal storm is set to impact the area Thursday.

"The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our city and agency partners, we've made the decision to move the celebration due to expected severe weather," Macy's said in a statement. "Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday."

"Created by Macy's colleagues since 1924 as a gift to our city and nation, our parade has brought magic into the hearts of millions and have created cherished memories that have spanned generations," Will Coss, executive producer and vice president of Macy's Branded Entertainment, said at a press conference Wednesday . "This year we marked our 100th march, a milestone built on creativity, celebration and tradition. While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our participants and spectators is and always will be our top priority."

"We know that our city is the greatest city in the world, and we also know that in our city, nothing comes easily, and you have to plan for every possibility," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "And while we were looking forward to celebrating Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow, extreme weather has forced us to reschedule for Saturday instead."
Mamdani pointed to the "heavy storm" expected Thursday, with wind gusts up to 65 mph possible, along with potential flash flooding.

"Now I know many New Yorkers, myself included as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," Mamdani said. "I know that this change of plan will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first. And on Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting, will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe."

"By moving the parade to Saturday when weather conditions are much more favorable, we can give New Yorkers the celebration that they've been looking forward to without compromising on safety," NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said.
The watchword for the mayor's office, the NYPD and Macy's is safety, and there's ample reason for concern. Past parades have seen balloons tear, deflate or collide with overhead wires.

In 1997, high winds pushed several balloons out of control. The Cat in the Hat balloon struck a lamppost near Central Park West, which brought down a heavy fixture, injuring four spectators. A woman suffered a fractured skull and coma. Barney and the Pink Panther balloons also ran into trouble and had to be deflated.

In 1993, Sonic the Hedgehog was driven by high winds into a lamppost, injuring spectators and an NYPD officer. Dudley the Dragon hit a lamppost in Columbus Circle in that same parade, ending glass showering down on the crowd.
In 1971, balloons were grounded because of high winds, but even during COVID, the parade went on.

"Our colleagues, our volunteers, our participants - we've spent over two years working on this very parade. This parade has been built with love, with creativity. Since 1924 we've had an opportunity to create memories, to bring joy to millions of people here in New York City. That is our top priority. We're saddened by this shift, but we're optimistic about our opportunity to deliver the most spectacular 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, the best and biggest parade in our history," Coss said. "We look forward to sharing it with all of New York and everyone else across the nation."

The operational challenges involved in shifting the date of the parade are substantial. The parade involves plenty of marching bands and other performers who had been expecting the event on Thursday, and now will need to make alternative arrangements.
Coss said they are in communication with all parade participants, including those who have come from out of state.

"We are optimistic that we're going to be able to maintain the parade that we set out to produce and to deliver to New York City on Thanksgiving," he said. "There's still some logistics to be worked out, but everyone understands what we're up against and is rallying behind us to create the best and most successful 100th parade."
There will not be a second Inflation Celebration event before Saturday's parade, Coss added.

"[The balloons] have to be prepared, which is a weeks-long process that's going to get condensed to about 24 hours, so the team's going to be hard at work preparing for Saturday," he said, "so by the time we're ready to deliver back to New York City, it's really about inflating and getting ourselves stepped off for a successful parade on Saturday."
Tisch added that the NYPD will have to call in over 1,000 officers who were previously scheduled to be off on Saturday to work the parade.
body_zh: 梅西百货周三表示，梅西百货感恩节游行历史上首次因天气原因推迟。
第 100 届年度游行将于周六上午 8:30 开始。
这一历史性举措发生之际，一场强大的沿海风暴将于周四影响该地区。
梅西百货在一份声明中表示：“参与者和观众的安全是我们的首要任务，在与我们的城市和机构合作伙伴密切协商后，由于预计的恶劣天气，我们决定推迟庆祝活动。” “感谢成千上万的志愿者、表演者和合作伙伴，他们每年创造了数百万人享受的魔法。我们期待着周六一起庆祝。”

梅西百货品牌娱乐执行制片人兼副总裁威尔·科斯 (Will Coss) 在周三的新闻发布会上表示：“自 1924 年以来，梅西百货的同事们一直在为我们的城市和国家打造礼物，我们的游行给数百万人的心中带来了魔力，并创造了几代人的珍贵回忆。” “今年我们庆祝了游行 100 周年，这是一个建立在创造力、庆祝活动和传统基础上的里程碑。虽然我们对游行被推迟感到心碎，但参与者和观众的安全始终是我们的首要任务。”
纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 表示：“我们知道，我们的城市是世界上最伟大的城市，我们也知道，在我们的城市，没有什么是轻而易举的，你必须为每一种可能性做好计划。” “虽然我们期待明天庆祝梅西百货第 100 届感恩节游行，但极端天气迫使我们改在周六举行。”
马姆达尼指出，周四预计将出现“强风暴”，阵风可能达到每小时 65 英里，并可能引发山洪。
马姆达尼说：“现在我知道许多纽约人，包括我自己以及世界各地数百万人，都期待着明天举行的游行。” “我知道这个计划的改变会带来不便，但安全必须放在第一位。周六，当气球升上天空时，每个纽约人和每个来访的人都将能够观看一场既真正壮观又安全的表演。”
纽约警察局局长杰西卡·蒂施说：“通过将游行移至天气条件更加有利的周六，我们可以在不影响安全的情况下为纽约人带来他们一直期待的庆祝活动。”
市长办公室、纽约市警察局和梅西百货的口号是安全，而且有充分的理由令人担忧。过去的游行中曾出现过气球撕裂、泄气或与架空电线相撞的情况。
1997年，大风使几个气球失控。戴帽子的猫气球撞到了中央公园西附近的一根灯柱，导致一个重型装置落下，导致四名观众受伤。一名妇女头骨骨折并处于昏迷状态。巴尼和粉红豹的气球也遇到了麻烦，不得不放气。
1993年，刺猬索尼克被大风吹到路灯柱上，导致观众和一名纽约警察局官员受伤。在同一次游行中，“龙达德利”撞上了哥伦布圆环的一根灯柱，导致玻璃洒落到人群中。
1971 年，气球因大风而搁浅，但即使在新冠疫情期间，游行仍在继续。
“我们的同事、我们的志愿者、我们的参与者 - 我们为这次游行花了两年多的时间。这次游行是用爱和创造力建造的。自 1924 年以来，我们有机会创造回忆，为纽约市数百万人带来欢乐。这是我们的首要任务。我们对这一转变感到悲伤，但我们对有机会举办最壮观的第 100 届梅西百货感恩节游行、最好、规模最大的游行感到乐观在我们的历史上，”科斯说。 “我们期待与整个纽约和全国其他人分享。”
改变游行日期所涉及的操作挑战是巨大的。游行中有大量行进乐队和其他表演者，他们原本期待周四的活动，但现在需要做出替代安排。
科斯说，他们正在与所有游行参与者保持联系，包括来自州外的人。
他说：“我们乐观地认为，我们将能够维持我们计划在感恩节制作并运送到纽约市的游行。” “还有一些后勤工作需要解决，但每个人都了解我们面临的挑战，并团结在我们身后，打造最好、最成功的第 100 届游行。”
科斯补充说，在周六的游行之前不会举行第二次通货膨胀庆祝活动。
“[气球]必须做好准备，这是一个长达数周的过程，最终会压缩到大约 24 小时，因此团队将努力为周六做准备，”他说，“因此，当我们准备好将气球送回纽约市时，真正的任务是充气并让我们为周六的成功游行做好准备。”
蒂施补充说，纽约警察局将不得不召集 1,000 多名原定于周六下班的警察来参加游行。

title_en: Questions linger about lead pollution from Iowa blast, despite officials’ assurances
title_zh: 尽管官员做出保证，但爱荷华州爆炸造成的铅污染问题仍然存在
summary: Scientists and Iowa residents said questions remain about how much contamination the Army’s detonation of lead azide caused, though they were hopeful about the initial results.
summary_zh: 科学家和爱荷华州居民表示，尽管他们对此抱有希望，但关于军队引爆叠氮化铅造成的污染程度仍然存在疑问
body_en: As federal officials offered reassurances Wednesday that the Army’s detonation of a cache of lead azide in Iowa produced a minimal plume of lead dust, independent scientists and local residents said questions remain about how much contamination the explosion caused, and where — though they were hopeful about the initial results.
Some people with homes closest to the blast who had heeded the call to evacuate said they were still unsure when it will be safe to return.

In a post on X around 5:30 p.m. local time , the Army said that the Federal Emergency Management Agency had issued an “all clear” around the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, where the detonation occurred, but provided little detail beyond that. “Post-detonation surface sampling is underway, and results will be released once complete,” it said.
Sean Byers, who lives across the street from the plant, said he plans to stay away from his home for a few days with his children.

“Although the Army has supposedly not detected lead in the air, I think it is in their best interest to make that claim,” he said. “I think that a lot of people in general are downplaying the potential long-term effects of what may be to come simply because they may have perceived the lead plume as less boisterous” than some had feared.

The Environmental Protection Agency said that initial, real-time air monitoring data — from four sites — had not detected any lead in the atmosphere; however, outside experts said it will take days to begin to understand whether there are hotspots that require cleanup.
Several experts said they were cautiously optimistic that the Army had averted the worst possible version of events in Middletown, Iowa.

The planned explosion, which occurred at 9 a.m. local time, had sparked an intense public outcry over the last two weeks. Local residents complained of poor communication from the Army and insufficient time to prepare — especially given the Thanksgiving holiday — which led officials to delay the detonation. Army leaders have said that detonating the 9,700 pounds of lead azide was the only option because the chemical had become so degraded and unstable that it was at risk of blowing up on its own.

Lead is a highly dangerous neurotoxin, and no level of exposure is considered safe. To assess where lead dust might have dispersed and how much contamination possibly occurred, academic and EPA scientists have spread out across Iowa to collect samples and begin testing.
A few more days of uncertainty about the risks lie ahead.

Dr. Joel Kaufman, a professor of medicine, epidemiology and environmental health sciences at the University of Washington who studies air pollution, said the EPA’s initial, real-time air monitoring was a promising sign but that it must be backed up with lab-based chemistry results from dust collected on the ground.
“This is a reasonable way to test for real-time lead in the environment,” he said, adding that it will be crucial to analyze samples from a wide variety of locations.
“Is it possible that they are right that the amount of lead that’s being put into the environment is virtually zero? Yes,” Kaufman said. “Is there reason to be suspicious about it? Yes.”
Andrew Whelton, a professor of civil, environmental and ecological engineering at Purdue University in Indiana, agreed that a study of physical samples is essential.
“You have to collect particles that deposit and send them to a lab for chemical analysis,” he said.
The EPA said Wednesday that it had 300 employees and contractors on the ground in Iowa and that they had taken 1,200 air, land and water samples before the detonation.
“We are very diligently working to immediately send the new post-event samples back to EPA labs,” the agency said on X.
Garrett Anthony, a Burlington resident who said his home is about 7 miles from the blast site, evacuated earlier this week.

“I’m really thrilled to see that the live monitoring by the EPA is showing zero lead in the air, but the ground testing is still very, very important to me, and I want to see what happens next,” he said. “I definitely care about the lasting effects.”
Anthony said he stored some soil in advance to use as a baseline in tests if necessary.
body_zh: 周三，联邦官员再次保证，陆军在爱荷华州引爆的叠氮化铅储藏室产生了极少量的铅尘，独立科学家和当地居民表示，尽管他们对初步结果抱有希望，但爆炸造成的污染程度和污染地点仍然存在疑问。
一些家中距离爆炸地点最近的居民表示，他们仍然不确定何时可以安全返回。
下午 5:30 左右在 X 上发表的一篇文章中当地时间，陆军表示，联邦紧急事务管理局已在发生爆炸的爱荷华州陆军弹药厂周围发布“警报解除”，但除此之外几乎没有提供任何细节。 “爆炸后表面采样正在进行中，结果将在完成后发布，”它说。
住在工厂街对面的肖恩·拜尔斯(Sean Byers)表示，他计划和孩子们一起离开家几天。
“虽然据称陆军没有检测到空气中的铅，但我认为做出这样的说法符合他们的最大利益，”他说。 “我认为，很多人普遍低估了未来可能发生的潜在长期影响，仅仅是因为他们可能认为铅羽流没有一些人担心的那么剧烈”。
美国环境保护局表示，来自四个地点的初步实时空气监测数据并未检测到大气中存在任何铅；然而，外部专家表示，需要几天时间才能开始了解是否存在需要清理的热点。
几位专家表示，他们对陆军已经避免了爱荷华州米德尔敦事件最糟糕的情况表示谨慎乐观。
计划中的爆炸发生在当地时间上午 9 点，过去两周引发了公众的强烈抗议。当地居民抱怨陆军沟通不畅，准备时间不足，尤其是考虑到感恩节假期，导致官员推迟了爆炸。陆军领导人表示，引爆 9,700 磅叠氮化铅是唯一的选择，因为这种化学物质已经降解且不稳定，有自行爆炸的危险。
铅是一种高度危险的神经毒素，任何水平的接触都被认为是安全的。为了评估铅尘可能散布的地方以及可能发生的污染程度，学术界和美国环保署的科学家已分散到爱荷华州各地收集样本并开始测试。
未来几天风险仍存在不确定性。
华盛顿大学研究空气污染的医学、流行病学和环境健康科学教授乔尔·考夫曼博士表示，美国环保局最初的实时空气监测是一个有希望的迹象，但它必须得到地面收集灰尘的实验室化学结果的支持。
他说：“这是一种实时测试环境中铅含量的合理方法。”他补充说，分析来自不同地点的样本至关重要。
“他们认为排放到环境中的铅量几乎为零，这可能是正确的吗？是的，”考夫曼说。 “有理由对此表示怀疑吗？是的。”
印第安纳州普渡大学土木、环境和生态工程教授安德鲁惠尔顿（Andrew Whelton）同意对物理样本的研究至关重要。
“你必须收集沉积的颗粒并将它们送到实验室进行化学分析，”他说。
美国环保署周三表示，在爱荷华州有 300 名员工和承包商，他们在爆炸前采集了 1,200 个空气、土地和水样本。
“我们正在非常努力地工作，立即将新的事件后样本送回 EPA 实验室，”该机构在 X 上表示。
伯灵顿居民加勒特·安东尼 (Garrett Anthony) 表示，他的家距离爆炸现场约 7 英里，已于本周早些时候撤离。
“我真的很高兴看到美国环保局的实时监测显示空气中的铅含量为零，但地面测试对我来说仍然非常非常重要，我想看看接下来会发生什么，”他说。 “我绝对关心持久的影响。”
安东尼说，他提前储存了一些土壤，以便在必要时用作测试的基线。

title_en: A Journey Through the Absurd Hell of Trump’s Third-Country Deportations
title_zh: 特朗普驱逐第三国的荒谬地狱之旅
summary: How a Thai-born, US-raised Cambodian refugee ended up a prisoner of Africa’s last absolute monarch.
summary_zh: 一名在泰国出生、在美国长大的柬埔寨难民如何最终成为非洲最后一位专制君主的囚犯。
body_en: The warden kept telling Pheap Rom not to think of himself as a prisoner. Instead, the jailer insisted, Rom and his fellow deportees from the United States were “the king’s guests.”

Here was the warden’s idea of royal hospitality: Each morning at 7:30, Rom—a chiseled, compact, 43-year-old Cambodian man with a pronounced Philly accent—was roused from a bare cell he shared with three other men in Eswatini, a tiny kingdom in Southern Africa . Then he was made to stand at attention as the country’s national anthem, “Nkulunkulu Mnikati Wetibusiso temaSwati,” reverberated through the halls of the Matsapha Correctional Centre. Most meals consisted of a portion of rice splashed with thin broth. It was late 2025, and the weather was warm and wet. For 15 minutes a day, Rom and the other men were allowed to go outside. Before they were locked up for lights out, the anthem played again; thick clouds of mosquitoes kept Rom thrashing all night.

Sometimes Rom would banter with the towering, bespectacled warden, who went by the name Kuenene. If I’m a guest, then why am I being held in a prison with criminals? Rom would ask. Why aren’t I allowed to leave? But Rom knew these exchanges with the warden were absurd, like everything else about his situation.

Before the second Trump administration, the practice of deporting immigrants to countries where they have no ties was a rare and tightly restricted move in US immigration enforcement —reserved mainly for cases where a person simply could not be returned to their nation of origin due to risk of persecution or torture. It has since expanded into a signature White House policy of mass removal. Over the past two years, the administration has inked deals with some 35 nations to accept third-country deportees from the US. The kingdom of Eswatini, which agreed to take up to 160 migrants for a fee of $5.1 million, is one of them. Some of the other destination countries—the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, South Sudan—are so violent and unstable that they rank on the State Department’s “Do Not Travel” list.
Pheap Rom's home in Eswatini. Photograph: Oupa Nkosi/Reuters

Often making a spectacle of its own transgressiveness, the administration has steamrolled past public outcry, an investigation by Democratic lawmakers, and a warning from the United Nations about a “cascade of human rights violations” resulting from these removals. At least twice in the past two years, US federal courts have ordered the Department of Homeland Security to stop shipping migrants to third countries with insufficient due process. Both times, the Supreme Court has quickly stepped in to let the administration resume.

In September, during one of those brief, court-ordered pauses in removal flights, DHS general counsel James Percival went on X to publish the most comprehensive figures yet on how many migrants have been affected by the practice. He posted a GIF of Taylor Swift mouthing the words “That’s my husband” and pointing excitedly at her wedding ring. Percival’s caption: “How my wife looks at me when I tell her we have deported 25,000 illegal aliens to third nations.”

Rather than slowing down in the face of resistance, in fact, President Trump’s third-country push appears to have inspired imitators. Five European Union countries announced in November that they are working toward a plan to send rejected asylum seekers to a deportation hub in ​Rwanda. In the past two years, Italy has begun sending asylum seekers to Albania. The United Kingdom quietly sent an asylum seeker to Eswatini earlier this year; the man, originally from Sri Lanka, died last month, the government of Eswatini reported. According to local media, the apparent cause was suicide.

Rom’s lawyer, Tin Thanh Nguyen—who is himself the child of refugees from Vietnam—predicts that, if the administration keeps getting away with these expulsions, additional wealthy countries will be emboldened to offload their undesirables to poorer nations for a price. “This is going to be the new model for the West, not only for the United States,” says Nguyen, who also represents three other men currently held in Eswatini and Rwanda. “It’s just kind of out of sight, out of mind for these Western countries.”

But as Rom’s experience reveals, some of these removals may rest on little more than bureaucratic fiction. The US claims it has followed due process with every one of the 25,000 migrants deported to unfamiliar lands. “Their own countries say, ‘We do not want them back,’” US attorney general Todd Blanche told Fox News in early October. Yet in Rom’s case—among countless other Kafkaesque details—his own country never even appears to have been asked.

An American in virtually everything but citizenship status, Rom came to the United States as a 3-year-old refugee from Cambodia. Around 1979, his parents fled their home to escape the horrors of the Khmer Rouge, a genocidal regime that seized power in the wake of Richard Nixon’s carpet-bombing of the country. From there, the family went to a Thai refugee camp—where Rom was born in 1982—and then to a resettlement center in the Philippines. As Rom’s father was selling off possessions to raise money for their ultimate move to America, he was killed by roadside thieves. Rom sat by his side after the attack, his mother later told him, trying to wake his father up.

Rom’s first memories of America are of a cramped, dimly lit bedroom in a small apartment in the Bronx, where he arrived with his mother and six siblings in 1985. “There was just one mattress, and we all slept on that,” he says. “It was a new world to us; everything was new.”

Rom and his family had arrived in the middle of the largest resettlement effort in US history. As America’s chimerical war efforts in Southeast Asia faltered in the 1970s, hundreds of thousands of people began arriving in the US from Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia. Of the nearly 158,000 Cambodians who gained entry between 1975 and 1994, the majority, like Rom and his family, were refugees deeply marked by the atrocities of the Khmer Rouge.

Around 10,000 of them came to be resettled in areas of the Bronx that were blighted by high crime and poverty. Many were placed in dilapidated housing, with limited job opportunities. Rom’s mother, who didn’t speak English, relied on government support checks and whatever extra income she could make sewing and scavenging. As a child, Rom would help her collect cans and carry the overstuffed bags to the grocery store to return for cash.

With the help of an uncle, the family eventually relocated to Philadelphia, where an adolescent Rom was enticed by a newly formed gang—a Cambodian clique within the Crips called the Blue Dragons. “If you don’t want to get bullied,” older members of the gang told him, “you need to link up with us.” Rom was barely a teenager. An older gang member dubbed him Menace, after Dennis the Menace, because he was “funny and bad at the same time.”
body_zh: 典狱长不断告诉 Pheap Rom 不要将自己视为囚犯。相反，狱卒坚称，罗姆和他的美国被驱逐者同伴是“国王的客人”。

典狱长对皇室款待的想法是这样的：每天早上 7 点 30 分，罗姆——一位轮廓分明、身材矮小、说话带有明显费城口音的 43 岁柬埔寨男子——被从他与另外三名男子共同居住在南部非洲小王国斯威士兰的一间空荡荡的牢房中叫醒。然后，当国家国歌“Nkulunkulu Mnikati Wetibusiso temaSwati”回荡在马萨帕惩教中心的大厅时，他被要求立正。大多数饭菜都是由一份米饭和稀汤组成的。那是2025年末，天气温暖湿润。罗姆和其他人每天被允许外出 15 分钟。在他们被关起来熄灯之前，国歌再次响起；密密麻麻的蚊子让罗姆整个晚上都在挣扎。
有时，罗姆会与身材高大、戴着眼镜的典狱长开玩笑，典狱长的名字叫库内内。如果我是客人，那为什么我会和罪犯一起关在监狱里？罗姆会问。为什么不让我离开？但罗姆知道与典狱长的这些交流是荒谬的，就像他处境的其他一切一样。

在特朗普第二届政府之前，将移民驱逐到与他们没有联系的国家的做法是美国移民执法中罕见且受到严格限制的举措——主要是针对因遭受迫害或酷刑的风险而无法将其返回原籍国的情况。此后，它已扩展为白宫标志性的大规模搬迁政策。过去两年，政府已与约 35 个国家签署协议，接受来自美国的第三国被驱逐者。斯威士兰王国就是其中之一，该国同意以 510 万美元的费用接收最多 160 名移民。其他一些目的地国家——中非共和国、刚果民主共和国、南苏丹——由于暴力和不稳定而被列入国务院的“禁止旅行”名单。
Pheap Rom 在斯威士兰的家。照片：Oupa Nkosi/路透社
政府经常炫耀自己的越轨行为，但它却平息了公众的强烈抗议、民主党议员的调查以及联合国关于这些驱逐行动造成的“一系列侵犯人权行为”的警告。过去两年中，美国联邦法院至少两次下令国土安全部在正当程序不充分的情况下停止向第三国运送移民。两次，最高法院都迅速介入，让政府恢复运作。

9月，在法院下令的遣送航班短暂暂停之一期间，国土安全部总法律顾问詹姆斯·珀西瓦尔（James Percival）在X网站上发布了迄今为止最全面的数据，说明有多少移民受到了这种做法的影响。他发布了泰勒·斯威夫特 (Taylor Swift) 的 GIF 动图，嘴里说着“那是我的丈夫”，并兴奋地指着她的结婚戒指。珀西瓦尔的说明文字：“当我告诉我的妻子我们已将 25,000 名非法外国人驱逐到第三国时，她是如何看待我的。”
事实上，特朗普总统在第三国的推动似乎并没有因为阻力而放慢脚步，反而激发了效仿者。五个欧盟国家于 11 月宣布，他们正在制定一项计划，将被拒绝的寻求庇护者送往卢旺达的驱逐中心。过去两年，意大利开始向阿尔巴尼亚派遣寻求庇护者。今年早些时候，英国悄悄向斯威士兰派遣了一名寻求庇护者。据斯威士兰政府报道，这名男子来自斯里兰卡，于上个月死亡。据当地媒体报道，明显原因是自杀。
罗姆的律师丁清阮（Tin Thanh Nguyen）本人就是越南难民的孩子。他预测，如果政府继续实施这些驱逐行为，更多的富裕国家将更有底气，有价地将不受欢迎的人出售给较贫穷的国家。阮说：“这将成为西方的新模式，而不仅仅是美国。”他也是目前被关押在斯威士兰和卢旺达的另外三名男子的代表。 “对于这些西方国家来说，这有点眼不见心不烦。”
但正如罗姆的经历所揭示的那样，其中一些撤职可能只不过是官僚主义的虚构而已。美国声称，在将 25,000 名移民驱逐到陌生土地的过程中，每一位都遵循了正当程序。 “他们自己的国家说，‘我们不希望他们回来’，”美国司法部长托德·布兰奇 10 月初告诉福克斯新闻。然而，在罗姆的例子中——以及无数其他卡夫卡式的细节——他自己的国家似乎从未被问过。

罗姆（Rom）作为一名三岁难民从柬埔寨来到美国，除了公民身份外，几乎拥有一切美国人身份。 1979 年左右，他的父母为了躲避红色高棉的恐怖而逃离家园。红色高棉是一个种族灭绝政权，在理查德·尼克松对该国进行地毯式轰炸后夺取了权力。从那里，一家人去了一个泰国难民营——罗姆于 1982 年出生在那里——然后又去了菲律宾的一个安置中心。当罗姆的父亲变卖财产为他们最终搬到美国筹集资金时，他被路边小偷杀害了。他的母亲后来告诉他，袭击发生后，罗姆坐在他身边，试图叫醒他的父亲。
罗姆对美国的最初记忆是布朗克斯一间小公寓里一间狭窄、灯光昏暗的卧室，他于 1985 年与母亲和六个兄弟姐妹来到这里。“只有一个床垫，我们都睡在上面，”他说。 “这对我们来说是一个新世界；一切都是新的。”
罗姆和他的家人来到这里，正在进行美国历史上最大规模的重新安置工作。 20 世纪 70 年代，随着美国在东南亚的空想战争努力动摇，数十万人开始从越南、老挝和柬埔寨抵达美国。 1975 年至 1994 年间入境的近 158,000 名柬埔寨人中，大多数像罗姆及其家人一样，都是深受红色高棉暴行影响的难民。
其中约 10,000 人来到布朗克斯区重新定居，那里的犯罪率高且贫困。许多人被安置在破旧的住房中，就业机会有限。罗姆的母亲不会说英语，她依靠政府的补助支票以及缝纫和拾荒赚取的任何额外收入。小时候，罗姆会帮助她收集罐头，然后把装满东西的袋子搬到杂货店换取现金。
在叔叔的帮助下，一家人最终搬到了费城，在那里，一个青少年罗姆人被一个新成立的帮派——一个名为“蓝龙”（Blue Dragons）的柬埔寨小团体——所吸引。 “如果你不想被欺负，”团伙中的年长成员告诉他，“你需要与我们联系。”罗姆还不到十几岁。一名年长的帮派成员以“威胁丹尼斯”的名字给他起了个“威胁”的绰号，因为他“既有趣又坏”。

title_en: Republicans’ midterm reckoning comes for the RNC
title_zh: 共和党的中期清算即将到来
summary: President Donald Trump’s handpicked chair is fending off a challenge from his own colleague as Republicans grapple with who should pay the price for midterm losses.
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统精心挑选的主席正在抵御来自他自己的同事的挑战，共和党人正在努力解决谁应该为这一目标付出代价的问题。
body_en: The chair of the Republican National Committee is scrambling to avoid becoming the party’s midterms scapegoat.

With President Donald Trump’s backing, Joe Gruters would normally be a lock to retain his position as RNC chair. But after this month’s brutal midterm losses, he is now trying to fend off an upstart and surprisingly strong challenge from co-chair KC Crosbie ahead of the January leadership election. As both candidates jockey behind the scenes for support, deep divisions have emerged between members over who bears responsibility for the wipeout earlier this month and what comes next.

Party leaders have been reluctant to publicly point fingers at Trump and his unpopular agenda. Instead, conversations with more than two dozen RNC members and operatives familiar with the committee’s dynamics reveal that some are channeling their frustration toward Gruters. Even as his supporters argue he’s being unfairly blamed for a difficult political environment, Gruters could still become the fall guy.
For some of Gruters’ critics, the decision is simple: Someone must pay for the once-unthinkable losses.

“It is time for new leadership. That's nothing against Joe at all,” said Kentucky GOP Chair Robert Benvenuti, who plans to vote for Crosbie. “But different times require different leadership, different types of leaders.”

An undecided RNC member added: “There's an awful lot of anger.” That member, granted anonymity to speak candidly about private conversations, described members questioning whether to “rubber stamp the guy that rightly or wrongly is seen as the architect of this mess.”

The debate within the RNC — whether to break with the Trump-backed candidate or stick with the status quo — mirrors the broader reckoning underway in the GOP over how closely to align with the president moving forward. Many Republicans have resigned themselves to Trump’s continued dominance over the next two years, but some RNC members have already begun to agitate for change in other ways, including by calling for an autopsy of the midterms and for congressional leadership elections to be delayed.

Several RNC members said Gruters helped the committee raise millions this cycle, arguing that alone is a key part of his job and he handled it well. Others were frustrated that the RNC didn’t engage or spend money in their states earlier. And some members criticized Gruters for allowing the RNC to become overly enmeshed in the White House’s political operation.

“The party raised a lot of money, and we spent it. I don't think that there's a whole lot of that that can be laid at [Gruters’] feet,” said West Virginia GOP chair Josh Holstein, who said he has not yet committed either way in the leadership race. “At the same time, I know there's a lot of members of the committee that feel we need to go a different direction, and that the RNC needs to be a little more autonomous in its decision making.”
The RNC and Crosbie declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.
The Gruters campaign said in a statement that RNC members “are rallying behind Chairman Gruters because they know he will never stop fighting for Republicans.”

“Chairman Joe Gruters has 25 years of experience at every level of the Republican Party, shattering fundraising records, building the largest election integrity operation in party history, and advancing President Trump’s agenda,” the campaign said.

The outcome of the leadership race, which will be determined by a secret ballot, will test just how far RNC members are willing to go to change course — even if it means defying Trump. And the stakes are enormous, with the RNC playing a key role in the presidential race, including running the GOP primary debates, hosting the party’s 2028 convention and supporting the eventual nominee.

Complicating the calculation is Trump’s own involvement: The president has been a vocal supporter of Gruters and has privately suggested that if Crosbie wins the leadership battle, he wouldn’t assist the RNC with fundraising ahead of 2028, according to two people familiar with the threat who were granted anonymity to speak about private details. The threat was first reported by Axios .
It’s an apparent acknowledgement that even Trump knows it’s a real contest — and that his chosen candidate may become a scapegoat.

Vice President JD Vance, who also serves as the RNC’s finance chair and is considering a presidential bid, has privately offered to assist Gruters’ reelection campaign, according to a person with direct knowledge of the outreach granted anonymity to speak about private details. Gruters has not yet taken Vance up on his offer, the person said.
Vance’s office did not respond to a request for comment.

“There is an element that is concerned about this underlying President Trump support, and if we don’t vote for his guy, we’re undermining the president and further giving him more bad news, black eyes, and there’s some sensitivities to that,” said a second RNC member who is undecided about the leadership election and granted anonymity to speak candidly about sensitive political dynamics.
“But you also have some that are more protective of the brand and the party than they are to the person, especially given the results of this last election cycle,” the person said.
Trump allies have been checking in with RNC members to gauge where they stand in the leadership race, said the RNC member, who received such a call.
body_zh: 共和党全国委员会主席正忙于避免成为该党中期选举的替罪羊。
在唐纳德·特朗普总统的支持下，乔·格鲁特斯通常会保住共和党全国委员会主席的职位。但在本月的中期选举惨败之后，他现在正试图在 1 月份领导人选举之前抵御来自联合主席 KC Crosbie 的新贵和令人惊讶的强大挑战。随着两位候选人在幕后争取支持，成员之间在谁应对本月初的这场惨败以及接下来会发生什么问题上出现了深刻的分歧。
政党领导人一直不愿公开指责特朗普及其不受欢​​迎的议程。相反，与熟悉委员会动态的两打共和党全国委员会成员和工作人员的对话显示，一些人正在将他们的沮丧情绪发泄到格鲁特斯身上。尽管他的支持者认为他因困难的政治环境而受到不公平的指责，但格鲁特斯仍然可能成为替罪羊。
对于格鲁特斯的一些批评者来说，决定很简单：必须有人为曾经难以想象的损失付出代价。
“现在是新领导层的时候了。这根本不反对乔，”肯塔基州共和党主席罗伯特·本韦努蒂说，他计划投票给克罗斯比。 “但不同的时代需要不同的领导力、不同类型的领导者。”
一位尚未做出决定的共和党全国委员会成员补充道：“人们非常愤怒。”这名不愿透露姓名的成员坦率地谈论了私人谈话，他描述了成员们质疑是否“对那个被正确或错误地视为这场混乱的始作俑者的人盖上橡皮图章”的问题。
共和党全国委员会内部的辩论——是与特朗普支持的候选人决裂还是坚持现状——反映出共和党正在就如何与总统保持一致进行更广泛的思考。许多共和党人已经接受特朗普在未来两年继续占据主导地位，但一些共和党全国委员会成员已经开始以其他方式鼓动变革，包括呼吁对中期选举进行尸检并推迟国会领导人选举。
几名共和党全国委员会成员表示，格鲁特斯帮助委员会在本周期筹集了数百万美元，并认为这本身就是他工作的关键部分，而且他处理得很好。其他人则对共和党全国委员会没有更早地在他们的州参与或花钱感到沮丧。一些成员批评格鲁特斯允许共和党全国委员会过度卷入白宫的政治运作。
西弗吉尼亚州共和党主席乔什·霍尔斯坦（Josh Holstein）表示，“该党筹集了很多钱，我们也花掉了。我不认为有那么多钱可以放在（格鲁特斯）脚下。”他表示，他还没有在领导竞选中做出任何承诺。 “与此同时，我知道委员会中有很多成员认为我们需要走不同的方向，共和党全国委员会在决策方面需要更加自主。”
共和党全国委员会和克罗斯比拒绝置评。白宫没有回应置评请求。
格鲁特斯竞选团队在一份声明中表示，共和党全国委员会成员“团结在格鲁特斯主席身后，因为他们知道他永远不会停止为共和党而战。”
竞选团队表示：“主席乔·格鲁特斯在共和党各个层面拥有 25 年的经验，打破了筹款记录，建立了党内历史上最大的选举诚信行动，并推进了特朗普总统的议程。”
领导人竞选的结果将通过无记名投票决定，这将考验共和党全国委员会成员愿意在多大程度上改变路线——即使这意味着反抗特朗普。赌注是巨大的，共和党全国委员会在总统竞选中发挥着关键作用，包括主持共和党初选辩论、主办该党 2028 年代表大会以及支持最终提名人。
特朗普本人的参与让计算变得更加复杂：据两位不愿透露姓名的知情人士透露，特朗普一直是格鲁特斯的直言不讳的支持者，并私下表示，如果克罗斯比赢得领导权之争，他不会在 2028 年之前协助共和党全国委员会筹款。该威胁最先由 Axios 报告。
这显然承认，就连特朗普也知道这是一场真正的竞争，而且他选择的候选人可能会成为替罪羊。
据一位不愿透露姓名的知情人士透露，副总统 JD 万斯 (JD Vance) 还担任共和党全国委员会的财务主席，正在考虑竞选总统，他私下表示愿意协助格鲁特斯的连任竞选。该人士称，格鲁特斯尚未接受万斯的提议。
万斯的办公室没有回应置评请求。
另一位共和党全国委员会成员表示：“有一个因素担心特朗普总统的潜在支持，如果我们不投票给他的人，我们就会削弱总统的地位，并进一步给他带来更多坏消息，这会带来一些敏感性。”另一位共和党全国委员会成员对领导人选举尚未做出决定，并要求匿名坦诚地谈论敏感的政治动态。
“但也有一些人对品牌和政党的保护程度高于对个人的保护程度，特别是考虑到上一个选举周期的结果，”该人士表示。
接到电话的共和党全国委员会成员表示，特朗普的盟友一直在与共和党全国委员会成员核实，以了解他们在领导竞选中的立场。

title_en: Trump faces looming wave of ICE lawsuits
title_zh: 特朗普面临迫在眉睫的 ICE 诉讼浪潮
summary: The Trump administration is facing the first of possibly hundreds of lawsuits testing whether it can be held liable for how immigration officers acted during the ICE crackdowns . Why it matters: These cases could force the administration to defend the conduct
summary_zh: 特朗普政府正面临可能数百起诉讼中的第一起，测试其是否应对移民官员的行为承担责任
body_en: The Trump administration is facing the first of possibly hundreds of lawsuits testing whether it can be held liable for how immigration officers acted during the ICE crackdowns .

Why it matters: These cases could force the administration to defend the conduct of officers operating under former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and now-retired Border Patrol Commander-at-large Greg Bovino.
Driving the news: Democracy Forward, an advocacy litigation nonprofit, filed its first Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA) case on Monday on behalf of Dayanne Figueroa.
Figueroa, a U.S. citizen, was arrested during Operation Midway Blitz in Chicago in October 2025.

Video footage of Figueroa's arrest, after dropping her son off at school, shows officers driving into her vehicle and dragging her out of her car by her legs in a chaotic scene with multiple witnesses.
Under FTCA, she could file for monetary compensation. And if the case goes to trial, discovery could reveal more information about the directives to make arrests during Operation Midway Blitz.

What they're saying: "I anticipated that I was going to be met with silence. I'm not surprised, but again, I still expect accountability, so I'm not gonna let that define the outcome of all this," Figueroa said in an exclusive interview with Axios. "I want my experience to be a catalyst for meaningful change."

Figueroa has also testified before Congress and filed a police report over her experience. She is now asking for no more than $1 million, according to the FTCA filing, which alleges unlawful arrest, battery and failure to provide medical care.

Zoom in: Figueroa's claim comes after filing an administrative complaint against DHS over its officers' conduct both during her arrest and while she was detained. The administration had six months to respond, but didn't, opening her path to an FTCA case.

"This is really a sort of tip of the spear of this type of case," Jeff Dubner, an attorney leading the effort for Democracy Forward, said of Figueroa's case. "We know of a number of administrative claims that are waiting for the time to ripen."

"As we are at the one-year mark for Midway Blitz, we are coming up in the one-year mark from Metro Surge [in Minneapolis], and also the broadening of the enforcement effort to really being around the country, and so, you know, we'll see more and more of these," he said.

The intrigue : Democracy Forward's legal team anticipates the government will try to dismiss Figueroa's case and others under tort law by claiming that the officers were acting within their discretion as law enforcement, her attorney Shiva Kooragayala said.
"There is no immunity for federal law enforcement officers who are carrying out immigration arrests or any other kinds of federal law enforcement," Dubner said.
"Congress was very intentional when it passed the FTCA, when it expanded the FTCA to include assault and battery and false arrest and false imprisonment by law enforcement officers."

The other side: " Federal agents who enforce our immigration laws, as they did in Operation Midway Blitz, which targeted criminal illegal aliens in Chicago, are protected by long-established legal immunities and defenses against lawsuits over their official conduct," a DOJ spokesperson said in a statement.

"The Federal Tort Claims Act is a limited waiver of sovereign immunity with strict requirements and exceptions, and filing a claim does not mean it has merit. We will respond to any litigation in court."
A DHS spokesperson said that its agents follow the laws passed by Congress.

Between the lines: Figueroa was recovering from a kidney surgery at the time, and the pressure of the officers pinning her to the ground caused her further complications. After asking for medical attention and then showing physical signs of distress, she began urinating blood while in custody. Figueroa was rushed to a hospital for treatment, according to the legal complaint.

"I'm so so grateful for having those people that were there to film. Like if they weren't there, this would have just gone under the rug." Figueroa said. "They took my DNA and everything, but I left the office with nothing, zero evidence, like I wasn't even there."
body_zh: 特朗普政府正面临可能数百起诉讼中的第一起，测试其是否应对移民官员在 ICE 镇压期间的行为承担责任。
重要性：这些案件可能迫使政府为前国土安全部部长克里斯蒂·诺姆和现已退休的边境巡逻司令格雷格·博维诺手下的官员的行为进行辩护。
推动这一消息的是：倡导诉讼非营利组织 Democracy Forward 于周一代表 Dayanne Figueroa 提起了第一起《联邦侵权索赔法》(FTCA) 案件。
菲格罗亚是一名美国公民，于 2025 年 10 月在芝加哥的中途岛闪电战行动中被捕。
菲格罗亚将儿子送到学校后被捕的视频显示，警察开车撞上她的车，抓住她的双腿将她从车里拖出来，场面混乱，有多名目击者。
根据 FTCA，她可以申请金钱赔偿。如果案件进入审判阶段，发现可能会揭示有关中途岛闪电战行动期间逮捕指令的更多信息。
他们在说什么：“我预料到我会遭到沉默。我并不感到惊讶，但我仍然期待问责制，所以我不会让这决定这一切的结果，”菲格罗亚在接受 Axios 独家采访时说道。 “我希望我的经历能够成为有意义的改变的催化剂。”
菲格罗亚还曾在国会作证，并就她的经历向警方提交了报告。根据 FTCA 的文件，她现在要求的赔偿不超过 100 万美元，指控非法逮捕、殴打和未能提供医疗服务。
放大：菲格罗亚的指控是在针对国土安全部官员在她被捕和被拘留期间的行为提出行政投诉后提出的。政府有六个月的时间做出回应，但没有做出回应，从而为她提起 FTCA 案件开辟了道路。
“这确实是此类案件的一个例子，”领导“民主前进”组织的律师杰夫·杜布纳在谈到菲格罗亚的案件时说道。 “我们知道有一些行政索赔正在等待时机成熟。”
他说：“中途岛闪电战已经一周年了，明尼阿波利斯的 Metro Surge 也即将迎来一周年，而且执法工作也将扩大到全国各地，所以，你知道，我们会看到越来越多的此类事件。”
阴谋：菲格罗亚的律师希瓦·库拉加亚拉 (Shiva Kooragayala) 表示，民主前进的法律团队预计，政府将试图根据侵权法驳回菲格罗亚的案件和其他案件，声称这些官员是在执法人员的酌处权范围内行事。
杜布纳说：“执行移民逮捕或任何其他类型联邦执法的联邦执法人员没有豁免权。”
“国会在通过 FTCA 时是非常有意的，当时它将 FTCA 的范围扩大到包括执法人员的攻击和殴打以及错误逮捕和非法监禁。”
另一方：“执行我们移民法的联邦特工，就像他们在针对芝加哥犯罪非法外国人的中途岛闪电战行动中所做的那样，受到长期确立的法律豁免权和针对其官方行为诉讼的辩护的保护，”司法部发言人在一份声明中表示。
“《联邦侵权索赔法》是对主​​权豁免的有限放弃，有严格的要求和例外，提出索赔并不意味着它有道理。我们将在法庭上回应任何诉讼。”
国土安全部发言人表示，其特工遵守国会通过的法律。
言外之意是：菲格罗亚当时正在从肾脏手术中恢复，警察将她按在地上的压力导致了她进一步的并发症。在寻求医疗救助并表现出痛苦的身体迹象后，她在拘留期间开始尿血。根据法律诉状，菲格罗亚被紧急送往医院接受治疗。
“我非常感谢那些在现场拍摄的人。如果他们不在那里，这件事就会被掩盖起来。”菲格罗亚说道。 “他们拿走了我的 DNA 和所有东西，但我什么都没有离开办公室，零证据，就像我根本不存在一样。”

title_en: Judge blocks FCC review of ABC station licenses for now
title_zh: 法官暂时阻止 FCC 对 ABC 电台许可证的审查
summary: The Walt Disney Co. secured a temporary restraining order Wednesday blocking the Federal Communications Commission from moving forward with an unusually early review of ABC’s broadcast-station licenses, which the media company has called an attack on free spee
summary_zh: 华特迪士尼公司周三获得了一项临时限制令，阻止联邦通信委员会推进一项不寻常的行动
body_en: Nov. 25, 2026, 7:45 PM EST / Updated Nov. 25, 2026, 9:06 PM EST

The Walt Disney Co. secured a temporary restraining order Wednesday blocking the Federal Communications Commission from moving forward with an unusually early review of ABC’s broadcast-station licenses, which the media company has called an attack on free speech by the Trump administration.

U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan’s decision is the latest turn in the legal battle between Disney and the FCC, the federal agency that regulates the broadcast airwaves. Disney filed a lawsuit against the FCC in August, calling the early license review an “existential threat” to the First Amendment.

The FCC “wants to stop, censor [and] control” what ABC can broadcast, Disney lawyer Beth Wilkinson told AliKhan at a hearing on Oct. 6. Wilkinson characterized FCC Chairman Brendan Carr’s actions as a series of “unending threats and retaliation.”
The FCC’s lawyers argued at the hearing that the U.S. District Court does not have jurisdiction in the matter, accusing ABC of trying to circumvent the federal regulatory process.
In her order Wednesday, the judge wrote that she concluded Disney was “likely to succeed on their retaliation claim” against the FCC.
The order blocks the agency “from taking any continuing or further action against Plaintiffs in relation to the early license renewal proceedings before the Federal Communications Commission.”
She also denied a request by the FCC to dismiss Disney’s lawsuits against the agency.
“This is not a close case,” AliKhan wrote, adding that the ABC stations “have a weighty interest” in vindicating their right to free speech without retaliation.

“Chairman Carr has taken President Trump’s rhetoric as his marching orders,” AliKhan wrote. The judge’s opinion and order referenced multiple social media posts by Trump in which he was critical of ABC. “Starting with expressions of hostility, President Trump has set his sights on Plaintiff ABC for several years now.”

In response to a request for comment, an FCC spokesperson said: “While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law — as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear.

“The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations,” the agency spokesperson added.
In a statement, an ABC News spokesperson cheered the temporary restraining order as an “important victory for the First Amendment.”

The courtroom confrontation stems from the FCC’s April 28 order directing Disney’s eight owned-and-operated TV stations to file their broadcast license renewals ahead of schedule. The licenses were not due to come up for renewal until 2028 at the earliest.

Carr has said that order was tied to the agency’s investigation into Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion practices . It came a day after Trump called on ABC to fire late-night host Jimmy Kimmel over a joke he had made about first lady Melania Trump.

AliKhan addressed the sequence of events following Kimmel’s joke, writing that “against the backdrop of President Trump and Chairman Carr’s call-and-response, it is no coincidence that President Trump criticized Mr. Kimmel’s skit on social media and the very next day Defendants initiated the early license renewal proceedings.”

The FCC is also reviewing whether ABC’s “The View” broke a requirement that broadcast stations give equal time to political candidates for the same office. Disney has argued that the talk show qualifies as a “bona fide news” program, meaning it is exempt from the equal-time rule.

In a phone interview with NBC News after Disney filed suit, Carr said he believed Disney’s challenge to the FCC’s order was a “meritless case.” In remarks at the agency’s open commission meeting last week, Carr said the suit was filed “in the wrong court” at “the wrong time.”

ABC Owned Television Stations, a division of Disney Entertainment Television, operates stations in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, Houston, San Francisco, the Raleigh-Durham area, and Fresno, California.

Anna Gomez, the lone Democrat on the FCC, said in a statement that AliKhan’s decision “shows that this FCC is a paper tiger whose threats crumble when challenged by those willing to defend their rights.”
body_zh: 美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 25 日晚上 7:45 / 更新于美国东部时间 2026 年 11 月 25 日晚上 9:06
华特迪士尼公司周三获得了一项临时限制令，阻止联邦通信委员会对美国广播公司的广播电台许可证进行异常早期的审查，该媒体公司称这是特朗普政府对言论自由的攻击。
美国地区法官洛伦·阿里汗 (Loren L. AliKhan) 的决定是迪士尼与监管广播电视的联邦机构 FCC 之间法律斗争的最新转折。迪士尼于 8 月对 FCC 提起诉讼，称早期许可审查对第一修正案构成“生存威胁”。
迪士尼律师贝丝·威尔金森 (Beth Wilkinson) 在 10 月 6 日的听证会上告​​诉阿里汗，FCC“想要阻止、审查和控制”ABC 的广播内容。威尔金森将 FCC 主席布伦丹·卡尔的行为描述为一系列“无休止的威胁和报复”。
FCC 的律师在听证会上辩称，美国地方法院对此事没有管辖权，指责 ABC 试图规避联邦监管程序。
法官在周三的命令中写道，她得出的结论是，迪士尼针对 FCC 的报复“很可能会成功”。
该命令阻止该机构“就联邦通信委员会的早期许可证更新程序对原告采取任何持续或进一步的行动。”
她还拒绝了联邦通信委员会驳回迪士尼对该机构诉讼的请求。
阿里汗写道：“这不是一个结案。”他补充说，美国广播公司电视台在维护言论自由权而不受报复方面“有着重大利益”。
“卡尔主席已将特朗普总统的言论作为他的前进命令，”阿里汗写道。法官的意见和命令引用了特朗普批评美国广播公司的多个社交媒体帖子。 “从表达敌意开始，特朗普总统多年来一直把目光投向原告 ABC。”
在回应置评请求时，联邦通信委员会发言人表示：“虽然我们赞赏地方法院部分拒绝迪士尼提出的初步禁令救济请求，但批准迪士尼动议的决定中的部分内容在事实和法律上都是错误的——正如最高法院的先例所表明的那样。”
“联邦通信委员会期待在此事上取得全面胜利。我们将继续利用我们的合法权力，让广播公司对其公共利益义务负责，”该机构发言人补充道。
美国广播公司新闻发言人在一份声明中称赞临时限制令是“第一修正案的重要胜利”。
这场法庭对峙源于 FCC 4 月 28 日的命令，要求迪士尼拥有和运营的八家电视台提前提交广播许可证续订申请。这些许可证最早要到 2028 年才会更新。
卡尔表示，该命令与该机构对迪士尼多元化、公平和包容性做法的调查有关。一天前，特朗普呼吁美国广播公司解雇深夜主持人吉米·金梅尔，因为他开了一个关于第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普的玩笑。
阿里汗谈到了金梅尔笑话后发生的一系列事件，他写道，“在特朗普总统和卡尔主席的呼唤和回应的背景下，特朗普总统在社交媒体上批评金梅尔先生的笑话，第二天被告就启动了提前许可证更新程序，这并非巧合。”
FCC 还在审查 ABC 的《The View》是否违反了广播电台为同一职位的政治候选人提供平等时间的要求。迪士尼辩称，该脱口秀节目符合“真正的新闻”节目的资格，这意味着它不受平等时间规则的约束。
迪士尼提起诉讼后，卡尔在接受 NBC 新闻电话采访时表示，他认为迪士尼对 FCC 禁令的质疑是“毫无根据的案件”。卡尔在上周该机构的公开委员会会议上发表讲话时表示，该诉讼是在“错误的时间”“向错误的法院”提起的。
ABC 旗下电视台是迪士尼娱乐电视台的一个部门，在纽约、洛杉矶、芝加哥、费城、休斯顿、旧金山、罗利-达勒姆地区和加利福尼亚州弗雷斯诺设有电视台。
FCC 中唯一的民主党人安娜·戈麦斯 (Anna Gomez) 在一份声明中表示，阿里汗的决定“表明 FCC 是一只纸老虎，当受到那些愿意捍卫自己权利的人的挑战时，它的威胁就会崩溃。”

title_en: At this Little Free Bakery in Austin, neighbors come for the pastries and stay for community connection
title_zh: 在奥斯汀的这家免费小面包店，邻居们前来品尝糕点，并留下来进行社区联系
summary: The bakers behind these pop-up pastry drops aren't raking in the profits, but they are building a space for people to come together in polarized times.
summary_zh: 这些弹出式糕点店背后的面包师并没有赚取利润，但他们正在为两极分化时代的人们聚集在一起创造一个空间
body_en: At this Little Free Bakery in Austin, neighbors come for the pastries and stay for community connection The bakers behind these pop-up pastry drops aren't raking in the profits, but they are building a space for people to come together in polarized times.

Nick Ruiz, who arrived at 7:15 in the morning to line up for the Free Bakery North Loop event, walks up to the table being run by baker and organizer Sarah Mason during the monthly gathering on Sunday, Sept. 6, 2026, in Austin, Texas. Michael Minasi/KUT News hide caption

AUSTIN, Texas— When lines form in parks they're usually for the playground. Kids taking turns on slides. Runners waiting to get a drink from a water fountain. But the line that forms in the Bruning Green park in Austin's North Loop neighborhood happens only once a month, always on the first Sunday, and includes people of all ages. They're all here for Sarah Mason's bakery.
Unlike other bakeries in town where a pastry can run upwards of $7, everything here is free.

Mason's popup is one of countless Little Free Bakeries across the country. The idea is similar to Little Free Libraries, the small boxes that are often set up in front yards where passersby can leave or take a book as they please. Instead of books, it's baked goods that are up for grabs.
Sarah Mason is the baker and organizer behind Free Bakery North Loop. She started holding the month events in September 2025. Michael Minasi/KUT News hide caption

Mason started the Free Bakery North Loop last September when she was working on improving her technical pastry skills. She was handing out baked goods at her job as an office leasing representative for WeWork, but soon she had more than she could give away.

She thought people would happen upon the event as they were walking through the neighborhood. But just in case, she posted on social media. That post took off and since then there has always been a line.

"I have a friend who jokes that waiting in the line is the most fun part, because everyone's excited and talking about what they're going to get when they get to the front of the line and you can meet people," Mason said.
People love a free treat, but Mason said she is pleasantly surprised at how many people stick around and hang out.

"It was unexpected," she said. "My observation of other free bakeries, it's more of a grab and go situation. But because we were in this park, it felt like there was room to spread out and room for other activities. It became more of a community event than just a free pastry."
Sarah Mason started the free bakery in her neighborhood after she found herself with a surplus of pastries when she was working on improving her baking skills.

For people like Sara and J.R. Almanza, the event hearkens back to old Austin, a time before the tech boom when the skyline had fewer skyscrapers and when the pace of life felt slower and it was easier to strike up a conversation with strangers. After attending the free bakery once, the Almanzas decided to come back and enjoy the sense of community.

"Right now it seems like people are becoming more divided. It feels like everything's so polarizing these days," J.R. said. "There's so much out there to kind of distract us from meeting people and engaging with other people, that events like this are important because it brings people together."
That sense of community is part of what led Lanne Stauffer to create the very first Little Free Bakery in Seattle in 2021.
Stauffer got the idea for a Little Free Bakery after she experienced a small act of kindness.
"We were still in the pandemic and the mood was scared and nobody was coming out of their houses and just a lot of fear in the air and there was a bouquet of flowers on my front step," Stauffer said.
body_zh: 在奥斯汀的这家免费小面包店，邻居们来这里品尝糕点，并留下来进行社区联系：NPR
尼克·鲁伊斯 (Nick Ruiz) 于早上 7:15 到达，排队参加免费面包店北环路活动，在 2026 年 9 月 6 日星期日在德克萨斯州奥斯汀举行的每月聚会期间，他走到面包师兼组织者莎拉·梅森 (Sarah Mason) 主持的桌子前。迈克尔·米纳西/KUT 新闻隐藏标题栏
德克萨斯州奥斯汀——当公园里排起长队时，通常是为了游乐场。孩子们轮流滑滑梯。跑步者等待从饮水机喝水。但奥斯汀北环路附近的布鲁宁格林公园每月只出现一次，而且总是在第一个周日，而且包括各个年龄段的人。他们都是来莎拉·梅森的面包店的。
与镇上其他面包店的糕点售价高达 7 美元不同，这里的一切都是免费的。
梅森的快闪店是全国无数小免费面包店之一。这个想法类似于小型免费图书馆，通常在前院设立小盒子，路人可以随意离开或拿走一本书。可供争夺的不是书籍，而是烘焙食品。
Sarah Mason 是 Free Bakery North Loop 背后的面包师和组织者。她从 2025 年 9 月开始举办每月活动。Michael Minasi/KUT News 隐藏标题栏
去年九月，梅森在努力提高自己的糕点技术时，创办了 Free Bakery North Loop。作为 WeWork 的办公室租赁代表，她负责分发烘焙食品，但很快她就​​收到了超出她所能分发的东西。
她认为人们在穿过附近时会看到这一事件。但为了以防万一，她在社交媒体上发布了这一消息。这篇文章开始流行，从那时起，就一直有人在排队。
梅森说：“我有一个朋友开玩笑说，排队等候是最有趣的部分，因为每个人都很兴奋，并谈论当他们到达队伍前面并且可以见到人们时他们会得到什么。”
人们喜欢免费的美食，但梅森说她很惊喜地发现有这么多人留下来闲逛。
“这是出乎意料的，”她说。 “根据我对其他免费面包店的观察，这更像是一种抢了就走的情况。但因为我们在这个公园里，感觉就像有空间可以展开，也有空间可以进行其他活动。它更像是一场社区活动，而不仅仅是免费的糕点。”
莎拉·梅森（Sarah Mason）在努力提高烘焙技巧时发现自己有多余的糕点，于是她在附近开了一家免费面包店。
对于像 Sara 和 J.R. Almanza 这样的人来说，这一事件让人回想起老奥斯汀，那是科技繁荣之前的时代，当时天际线的摩天大楼较少，生活节奏较慢，与陌生人交谈更容易。去过一次免费面包店后，阿尔曼萨一家决定回来享受社区的感觉。
“现在人们似乎变得更加分裂。感觉现在一切都如此两极分化，”J.R. 说。 “有太多事情分散了我们与人见面和与其他人交往的注意力，像这样的活动很重要，因为它让人们聚集在一起。”
这种社区意识促使 Lanne Stauffer 于 2021 年在西雅图创建了第一家 Little Free Bakery。
斯塔弗在经历了一次小小的善举后萌生了开一家小免费面包店的想法。
斯托弗说：“我们仍然处于大流行之中，人们的心情很害怕，没有人走出自己的房子，空气中弥漫着恐惧，我的门前台阶上有一束鲜花。”

title_en: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
title_zh: OpenAI 表示，随着 Chat 和 Work 的合并，ChatGPT 的大量用户可能会更快达到极限
summary: OpenAI will introduce a single usage meter across ChatGPT as it combines the Chat and Work experiences.
summary_zh: OpenAI 将在 ChatGPT 中引入单一使用计量表，因为它结合了聊天和工作体验。
body_en: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work | TechCrunch
OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage.

Under the new system, Chat and Work will share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, the OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch. Conversations using the Instant model will, however, remain unlimited and will not count toward the shared allowance. Users can also continue using Instant after exhausting their usage limits. The spokesperson added that OpenAI would continue working to improve efficiency so subscribers could get more out of their plans.
While the rollout has started for a small group of users, OpenAI plans to bring shared usage limits more broadly in December, per its support page.
Similar to OpenAI, rival Anthropic also moved to bring its conversational chat service Claude and work-focused Cowork under one interface in September.

The changes come as AI companies face mounting infrastructure costs and growing demand for increasingly capable models, putting pressure on their computing resources. Bringing conversational and work-related tools into a single interface could also make AI chatbots simpler to use, allowing users to move between chats and more complex tasks without switching tabs.

OpenAI 已开始在 ChatGPT 中向部分用户推出统一的聊天和工作体验，但一些用户批评合并可能会限制他们的使用。
OpenAI 发言人告诉 TechCrunch，在新系统下，聊天和工作将在 ChatGPT 上共享一个使用计量表。但是，使用即时模型的对话将不受限制，并且不计入共享限额。用户还可以在用尽使用限制后继续使用 Instant。该发言人补充说，OpenAI 将继续努力提高效率，以便订阅者可以从他们的计划中获得更多收益。
虽然该功能已开始针对一小部分用户推出，但根据其支持页面，OpenAI 计划在 12 月份更广泛地引入共享使用限制。
与 OpenAI 类似，竞争对手 Anthropic 也于 9 月份将其对话式聊天服务 Claude 和以工作为中心的 Cowork 纳入一个界面。
这些变化发生之际，人工智能公司面临着基础设施成本不断上升以及对功能日益强大的模型的需求不断增长，这给它们的计算资源带来了压力。将对话和工作相关工具引入单一界面还可以使人工智能聊天机器人更易于使用，允许用户在聊天和更复杂的任务之间移动，而无需切换选项卡。
